items.title: 2027: Nigeria needs reset, not reforms — Makinde
items.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Oyo State Governor and presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples’ Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has said Nigeria needs a fundamental reset rather than mere reforms to address its economic, security and governance challenges ahead of the 2027 general elections. Makinde spoke on Sunday during a live political programme on Jay FM 101.9 in Jos, Plateau State, ahead of the party’s presidential campaign flag-off scheduled for Monday in the city. Explaining his position, the governor argued that reforms were insufficient where the problems in a system outweighed its strengths. “When you talk about reform, it means that there is something good in the system that you want to improve upon. But when the bad outweighs the good, you need to take a different course of action. “If what you have in the system is only about 20 per cent of what you expected, you don’t need to continue tweaking it. You need to press the reset button, shut it down and reboot it. That is what Nigeria needs at this point. Reform will not work in the present environment,” he said. The governor said he did not initially intend to become a politician but was motivated by concerns about the country’s future. “I am not a career politician. I came into politics because I believe that the future of millions of Nigerians is at stake. We have the potential to become the greatest Black nation on the face of the earth, but we must make the right decisions to achieve that destiny,” he said. On the economy, Makinde identified it as the foremost priority of his proposed Reset Agenda, arguing that economic performance should be measured by improvements in the living conditions of ordinary Nigerians. “The economy must work for everybody. We should not just be talking about foreign reserves, World Bank figures or inflation statistics. What matters is whether ordinary Nigerians can afford to feed themselves and meet their basic needs,” he said. He added that economic progress should be assessed by its impact on households rather than statistical indicators alone. “If the people on the streets are not feeling any improvement, then we cannot say that the economy is doing well. The real test of economic performance is the condition of the people,” he said. The APM candidate said his proposed administration would prioritise skills acquisition, entrepreneurship, education and production, while creating an enabling environment for businesses to grow and generate employment. “We must encourage our people to acquire skills and become entrepreneurs. We must invest in education and move towards intensive production. Government must provide an environment where businesses can thrive and young people can find meaningful employment,” he said. On insecurity, Makinde advocated decentralising Nigeria’s security architecture through the establishment of state police, arguing that states should be allowed to adopt the arrangement when they are ready and necessary safeguards are in place. “I believe that we need to decentralise our security architecture. State police is one of the ways to achieve this, but it must be properly structured. States that are ready should be allowed to establish their own police formations, while others can come on board when they are prepared,” he said. Recalling his engagement with former President Muhammadu Buhari on the issue in 2019, Makinde said the former president had expressed concerns about the ability of some states to finance their own police formations. “When we approached President Buhari in 2019, one of the concerns he raised was that some states could not even pay workers’ salaries. He questioned how such states would be able to fund state police,” he said. He explained that governors in the South-West subsequently adopted the Western Nigeria Security Network, popularly known as Amotekun, as an alternative arrangement to strengthen security in the region. “We decided to find a middle ground through Amotekun. The operatives gather intelligence and work with the federal security agencies. It has helped to improve security coordination in the region,” he said. Makinde acknowledged concerns that state police could be abused by governors to intimidate political opponents and ordinary citizens but insisted that appropriate safeguards could address such risks. “We must not pretend that there are no concerns. Some people are worried that governors could use state police to oppress their opponents or intimidate citizens. Those concerns are valid, and we must put safeguards in place. “But the fact that something can be abused does not mean we should not do it. We must design a system that ensures accountability and protects the rights of the people,” he said. On Nigeria’s growing population, the governor warned that failure to provide opportunities for young people could worsen insecurity and social instability. He said the country could have a population of more than 300 million, with over 70 per cent below the age of 34, stressing the need to create opportunities for the youthful population. “If we fail to provide pathways for them to succeed, we should not be surprised when some of them turn to crime or other activities that threaten the stability of the country,” he said. Makinde also cited Nigeria’s gradual transition to self-government and independence as an example of how different parts of the country could adopt new arrangements at different times. “We had self-government in 1957 and independence in 1960. We did not achieve everything at once. In the same way, states do not necessarily have to establish state police at the same time. Those that are ready can begin, provided the necessary safeguards are in place,” he said. Recalling his handling of the COVID-19 lockdown in Oyo State in 2020, the governor said he opposed a blanket shutdown because of the hardship it could impose on residents who depended on daily earnings for survival. “I remember that during COVID-19, there was a proposal for a mandatory lockdown. I raised the concern that many people depended on what they earned each day to feed their families. If you locked them down completely, what would they eat that night or the following morning?” he said. He maintained that decisions on public health and governance should be guided by science, data and logic, while taking into account the realities of ordinary citizens. “We had to look at the situation and make decisions based on science, data and logic. We also had to understand the realities of our people. Some people were more worried about dying of hunger than the risk of contracting COVID-19,” he said. On education, Makinde praised the legacy of the late nationalist and statesman, Chief Obafemi Awolowo, particularly his free education policy, which he said expanded opportunities for generations of Nigerians. “Chief Awolowo understood that education was an investment in the future. The cocoa farmers paid their taxes, and the government used the resources to provide free education for children. “Those children grew up, became professionals and contributed to society. That is the kind of investment we must make in our people,” he said. The governor said his proposed administration would also prioritise honesty, transparency and accountability in the management of public resources. “The first thing I will do is to tell Nigerians the truth about the state of the country. People deserve to know where we are and what needs to be done. “The next thing is accountability. If you have accountability, then the chances are that public resources will be used for the benefit of the people,” he said. items.title: Customs processes 99,839 cargo declarations in two months
items.description: By Godwin Oritse The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) processed 9,195 Pre-Arrival Assessment Reports (PAARs) and 99,839 Single Goods Declarations (SGDs) between September and October 2026, generating a combined revenue of approximately ₦1.42 trillion. The figures were disclosed during a joint security press briefing at the National Counter Terrorism Centre (NCTC), under the Office of the National Security Adviser, in Abuja. Speaking at the briefing, the National Public Relations Officer of the NCS, Deputy Comptroller Abdullahi Aliyu Maiwada, said the performance reflected the Service’s commitment to facilitating legitimate trade, improving cargo clearance and strengthening revenue generation through digital interventions and collaboration with stakeholders. A breakdown of the figures showed that the Service processed 2,102 PAARs in September and 7,093 in October, bringing the total to 9,195. Similarly, 48,832 SGDs were processed in September, while 51,007 were recorded in October, giving a combined total of 99,839 declarations. The Service collected ₦697.8 billion in revenue in September and ₦722.9 billion in October, amounting to ₦1.4207 trillion during the two-month period. In a statement, Maiwada also disclosed that the Service recorded significant progress in export trade facilitation. At the Lilypond Export Command, export activities in the third quarter of 2026 generated a total export value of $752.85 million, compared with $586.15 million recorded in the corresponding period of 2025. The statement put the increase at approximately 28.44 per cent, reflecting the growing contribution of the export sector and the impact of measures aimed at facilitating non-oil exports. On enforcement, the NCS said it seized prohibited and restricted items with a combined Duty Paid Value exceeding ₦8.1 billion during the period under review. The interceptions covered various categories, including illicit drugs, pharmaceutical products, prohibited goods and petroleum products. The Service said it continued to collaborate with relevant regulatory and security agencies to ensure the appropriate handling and disposition of seized items. On its anti-money laundering and counter-financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) responsibilities, the NCS highlighted the ongoing World Customs Organisation (WCO) Mentoring Mission, inaugurated on October 19, 2026. The four-week engagement, scheduled to run from October 18 to November 13, 2026, is designed to strengthen the capacity of the Service to identify, investigate and tackle trade-based money laundering and other illicit financial activities associated with cross-border trade. As part of the exercise, the NCS engaged six relevant agencies between October 27 and 29, including the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), the Nigeria Financial Intelligence Unit (NFIU) and the National Counter Terrorism Centre. The Service also disclosed that it had transitioned to an electronic currency declaration platform as part of efforts to improve transparency, strengthen monitoring and enhance the detection of illicit financial flows across the country’s borders. In another development, the NCS said six live pangolins were rescued in separate operations in Ogun State during the period. Three were rescued by the Ogun I Area Command, while another three were intercepted by the Federal Operations Unit, Zone A. The animals were subsequently handed over to the Green Fingers Wildlife Conservation Initiative for care and rehabilitation in line with Nigeria’s obligations under the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES). items.title: Governorship Debate: Private sector cannot solve Lagos housing crisis alone – NDC’s Doherty
items.description: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate in Lagos State, Funso Doherty, has said the private sector cannot independently address the state’s housing crisis, urging the government to take a leading role in providing affordable accommodation. Doherty made the remarks during the Lagos governorship debate held in Lagos on Sunday and organised by the Nigeria Debate Consortium, comprising Channels Television, TVC News, The PUNCH, TheCable and Vanguard. Doherty outlined his proposals for tackling arbitrary rent increases and improving access to affordable housing. He described arbitrary rent increases in Lagos as a form of racketeering and promised to establish an ombudsman office to address complaints and protect tenants if elected. “There is a form of racketeering. We would set up an ombudsman office to deal with this,” he said. The NDC candidate identified inadequate housing supply as one of the major factors driving rising rents in the state, arguing that housing development had failed to keep pace with growing demand. “The larger solution of the problem is due to supply. Housing supply has not kept up with growing demand,” he said. Doherty maintained that social housing should be a major government responsibility, noting that private developers alone could not meet the accommodation needs of Lagos residents. “Social housing, that is an area, where government has to be the primary driver, private housing will not do it alone,” he added. He also criticised the state government for allegedly failing to make sufficient investments in areas requiring public intervention, arguing that it had allowed the private sector to take the lead in areas where government should play a more prominent role. “One of the areas we have a problem with this government is that they don’t step up in a big way in things they should, instead allow the private sector take the lead,” he said. items.title: Perhaps Connecting Fridges to the Internet Was a Bad Idea
items.description: Bags of frozen blueberries and Swedish meatballs, packets of waffles and pizzas, and tub after tub of ice cream: all melted, floppy, spoiled, and stinking. This has been the scene at grocery stores across Europe after their fridges and freezers have been hacked. Last month, employees at hundreds of supermarkets in France came into work to find they had to trash millions of dollars’ worth of food. The machines were not simply deactivated; they had been remotely hijacked and reprogrammed to hit temperatures as high as 122 degrees Fahrenheit. Last Monday, grocery outlets in at least seven more countries, including Estonia, Belgium, and Sweden, experienced a near-identical incident. The same day, freezers at the French national blood bank were also hacked (though staffers were able to intervene before any samples were corrupted). Depending on who you talk with, America is either next or has already been hit: In August, the Pentagon quietly revealed that freezers at commissaries on several U.S. military bases had malfunctioned in a suspected attack. No one has claimed responsibility for any of these exploits, and it’s not even clear whether they are connected. The hackers seemingly didn’t have a goal besides sowing chaos and wasting an enormous amount of food. Perhaps the most surprising aspect of these widespread fridge attacks is that they haven’t happened sooner. For hackers, these appliances make perfect targets. The basic problem is that many fridges and freezers are now connected to the internet. “The attacks are very simple,” Nadiya Kostyuk, a cybersecurity researcher at Carnegie Mellon University, told me. Each unit has a microcontroller that is connected to the local network, so even someone sitting at a computer thousands of miles away can theoretically access it. These devices are typically password protected, but they still tend to be pretty easy to crack, Kostyuk explained. “Usually it’s done by brute force,” which is to say the devices are spammed with password after password until one works. Some of the recent attacks were made simpler because usernames and passwords had never been changed from the manufacturer’s defaults. Once the hackers remotely broke into a system, they were able to take control of a heating element that can be periodically switched on to prevent frost from building up on the evaporator coils, which stops the freezer from working as effectively. Instructed to run repeatedly, that heating element has proved capable of cooking perishable food. For a home fridge, the benefits—a touchscreen that can show family photos, an interior camera so you can see what you already have while you’re at the grocery store—may not outweigh the security risks. In the aftermath of the recent attacks, people have assumed the same is true for industrial fridges: Why on earth does a supermarket fridge need to be online? But for the millions of supermarket chill cabinets, refrigerated trucks and shipping containers, and gigantic cold-storage warehouses that our food sits in on its way from farm to table, the calculus is quite different. Logistics companies are often required to demonstrate that food has stayed within a narrow temperature range while in their custody; the ability for a freezer to broadcast an alert if its temperature deviates from a set point at 2 a.m. is an extremely useful feature. Refrigeration units are always on—they have to run 24/7 by design—and a lot of today’s smartest devices provide the diagnostics that allow companies to perform predictive maintenance to preempt any potential issues. “The risk of loss is so high if the unit goes down,” Chris Gaffney, a supply-chain expert at Georgia Tech who previously ran logistics for Coca-Cola, told me. The food that our fridges are protecting is extremely fragile; the machines themselves are quite complex; and qualified technicians are in short supply. A refrigerated warehouse, let alone a supermarket, won’t have a person with that kind of specialist skill set on-site, Gaffney said. But when connected to the internet, a scattered portfolio of freezers can be managed and sometimes even fixed remotely. And, as politicians push legislation to make food traceable, the entire supply chain is being digitized. “There are a lot of positives that come with that—ways to increase our food security and understanding where food is coming from,” Sara Stickler, the president of the Global Cold Chain Alliance, an industry trade group, told me. “But with digitization, there also comes risks.” The food business isn’t like banking, where online security is central to a company’s value proposition. In perishable logistics, where the mission is keeping food cold, warehouse operators and grocery stores have not typically seen the value in spending extra on cybersecurity. “Margins are tough,” Gaffney said. When it comes to adopting sophisticated new technology, he told me, “logistics is a laggard, and within logistics, cold is a laggard.” The genius and horror of hacking refrigeration is that although the cold chain is essential infrastructure, it’s not treated as such. As I quickly learned while writing Frostbite , my recent book on the topic, almost no one has a complete picture of refrigeration’s scope and scale. Nearly three-quarters of everything on the American plate passes through the cold chain on its way to our tables. Thousands of chilled warehouses, refrigerated containers and trucks, meat lockers, and banana-ripening rooms are located out of sight, underground, at ports, near freeway intersections or cattle ranches: Added together, these pockets of artificial winter form the invisible backbone of our food system. Meanwhile, refrigeration is somehow different from other crucial infrastructure—water-treatment plants, say, or power stations—where the public may be ignorant, but at least industry members and government officials are on top of how many facilities we have and where they are. As supermarket shelves emptied during the early days of COVID, one industry expert told me that he received a frantic call from a senior official in the government asking how many refrigerated trucks and warehouses the country’s food supply depended on. If there is a silver lining to these attacks, it is that they could serve as a wake-up call. “With these cyberattacks, it totally redefines what ‘critical infrastructure’ is,” Kostyuk said. After all, cyberattacks are not the only threat facing our food-supply chain: Dozens of supermarket refrigerators across the U.K. failed this summer during a heatwave that pushed them beyond their limits, and severe-weather-induced blackouts are a constant threat. Whether the culprit is a hacker or the weather, the outcome remains the same. Get used to seeing more empty supermarket shelves.

items.title: Debate: ‘Lagos must learn from Japan, Venice to tackle flooding’ – GRV
items.description: The African Democratic Congress (ADC) governorship candidate in Lagos State, Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour, has criticised the state government over its approach to infrastructure development, traffic management and urban planning, saying the city needs visionary leadership to address its challenges. Rhodes-Vivour, popularly known as GRV, made the remarks during the Lagos governorship debate held in Lagos on Sunday and organised by the Nigeria Debate Consortium, comprising Channels Television, TVC News, The PUNCH, TheCable and Vanguard. GRV outlined his proposals for improving infrastructure and preparing the state for climate-related challenges. He argued that Lagos should learn from other coastal cities, including Japan and Venice, in developing infrastructure that accommodates water flow and reduces the impact of flooding. “We lack visionary govt. They should be looking at what Japan is doing, Vernice is doing, they are coastal cities too. Vernice is standing on trees, but allows for water to flow,” he said. The ADC candidate also questioned the quality of road construction in Lagos, arguing that infrastructure projects should meet proper technical standards and include long-term maintenance plans. “What are the standards of road we are building in this city? Roads are not built to standard. We need to set proper standards and technicalities, and tie in maintenance to the construction of those road,” he said. Rhodes-Vivour further called for climate scenario planning and better communication between the government and residents to prepare Lagos for future environmental challenges. On traffic congestion, he said residents should not have to spend excessive time commuting to work, calling for an integrated transportation system that connects different parts of the state. “Traffic is not a lifestyle, we must not have to work to get to work. We need to connect the entirety of Lagos. It is a bankable project that will pay itself over the years,” he said. He proposed expanding water transportation through functional ferry terminals and increasing the availability of ferry services across the state. “We need to normalise water transportation, have ferry terminals that are not just audio, have enough water transportation. We need to normalise bicycle lanes,” he added. The ADC candidate said improved water transportation and dedicated bicycle lanes would provide residents with more commuting options and help ease pressure on Lagos roads. items.title: 2027: Sokoto PDP backs Tinubu’s re-election bid
items.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Sokoto State has declared support for President Bola Tinubu’s second-term ambition, disclosing that it is negotiating a political alliance with the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) through the Nyesom Wike-led Rainbow Coalition ahead of the 2027 general elections. The PDP governorship candidate in the state, Abubakar Abdullahi Sokoto, disclosed this at a stakeholders’ meeting held at the party’s secretariat along Bodinga Road, Sokoto metropolis. Abdullahi said the proposed arrangement was aimed at mobilising support for Tinubu’s re-election, declaring that the PDP in Sokoto had no alternative presidential candidate apart from the incumbent president. “Our position is to work towards President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s second-term ambition through the Rainbow Coalition, which we consider a strategic political platform for cooperation between interested PDP stakeholders and the ruling APC,” he said. He, however, maintained that the alliance would not require the PDP to abandon its political structure or candidates contesting elective positions in the state. According to him, the party would continue to mobilise support and campaign for its candidates in the 2027 elections. “We are not abandoning our party structure or our candidates. We will continue to mobilise, canvass and campaign aggressively for PDP candidates seeking elective positions across Sokoto State in 2027,” he said. Abdullahi explained that in areas where PDP candidates might lack sufficient electoral support, party members and supporters could be encouraged to support APC candidates in line with the coalition arrangement. “Where our candidates may not have the necessary electoral strength or sufficient support, our members and supporters could be encouraged to support APC candidates as part of the political understanding under the Rainbow Coalition,” he stated. He said the arrangement was intended to strengthen political cooperation and improve the electoral prospects of parties and individuals involved in the coalition. Abdullahi added that the Rainbow Coalition remained open to political groups, organisations and individuals willing to identify with its objectives, irrespective of their party affiliations. “The Rainbow Coalition is open to everybody, political groups, organisations and individuals who share our vision and are prepared to identify with its objectives, irrespective of their political backgrounds,” he said. The PDP governorship candidate also appealed to former Vice President Atiku Abubakar to reconsider his presidential ambition and support Tinubu’s re-election bid by joining the emerging alliance. “I want to appeal to former Vice President Atiku Abubakar to reconsider his position and join this emerging political understanding rather than pursue an opposition agenda against President Tinubu’s second-term ambition,” he said. He argued that the proposed alliance provided an opportunity for broader consultations and political cooperation, urging political leaders to prioritise collective interests over partisan differences. The declaration signals a possible political realignment in Sokoto State, where the PDP is seeking to combine its independent ambitions in state elections with support for Tinubu’s presidential bid. However, the extent to which the proposed arrangement will shape the party’s electoral strategy at the state and national levels remains unclear as consultations continue. The development also raises questions about the PDP’s opposition role in Sokoto and the implications of the Rainbow Coalition for the party’s relationship with the APC ahead of the 2027 elections. items.title: Atlético de Madrid - Barcelona en directo, La Liga en vivo | El Barça se impone en el Metropolitano con un doblete de Fermín
items.description: El Barcelona superó este domingo al Atlético de Madrid en el Metropolitano en el broche final de una jornada en la que estaba en juego el liderato, que finalemente mantiene el Barça. El grupo de Diego Pablo Simeone empezó muy bien, pero Joan García frustó el mano a mano de Julián Alvarez y Pubill estampó su testarazo en el larguero. Los azulgrana contestaron con otro disparo a la madera de Lamine Yamal antes de que Giuliano marcara el primero a pase de Julián. Fermín empató el encuentro justo antes del descanso y completó la remontada en el segundo tramo tras una asistencia fantástica de Lamine. Los de Simeone recibían al líder, un Barcelona que perdió hace dos jornadas contra el Real Madrid en el Camp Nou, y que se mantiene en la tabla con 33 puntos, por los 28 del Atleti y los 30 de los blancos, que ayer derrotaron al Valencia en Mestalla. El equipo catalán marchaba impoluto en Liga hasta ese clásico que, además, se unió a la derrota contra el PSG en Champions. Uno de los alicientes del choque ha sido ver a Julián enfrentarse de nuevo al Barcelona después de que el delantero rojiblanco intentara fichar por el club azulgrana el pasado verano, un intento de traspaso al que se opuso el Atlético y que le ha costado esta temporada el reproche del Metropolitano. El ariete argentino erró dos mano a mano ante Joan García.

items.title: PML-N retains both Gujranwala's NA-77 and Sahiwal's PP-203, unofficial results show
items.description: LAHORE: The ruling PML-N retained Gujranwala’s National Assembly constituency NA-77 and Sahiwal’s Punjab Assembly constituency PP-203 in Sunday’s by-election. Both seats had fallen vacant after the deaths of their respective lawmakers in September. Polling in the constituencies began at 8am and concluded at 5pm, with the Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) reporting an uninterrupted and largely peaceful process. In NA-77, PML-N candidate Rashid Basheer Virk was among 11 candidates contesting for the seat left vacant after the Sept 11 demise of his father, Chaudhry Mehmood Bashir Virk, a five-time MNA. He secured victory by bagging 43,365 votes, while Pakistan Markazi Muslim League’s (PMML) Mohammad Ibrahim remained runner-up with 30,218 ballots, according to the Form-47 seen by Dawn. Form-47 is the provisional consolidated statement of results of the vote count of all polling stations in a constituency, prepared by the returning officer (RO) concerned. In PP-203 of Chichawatni, PML-N’s Muhammad Asad Hanif Jutt won with 42,114 votes, defeating his closest rival, Muhammad Awais Mahmood of Tehreek-i-Ehsas Pakistan (TEP), who secured 24,512 votes, according to its Form-47. Both by-elections were marked by a low voter turnout, with 15.7 per cent in NA-77 and 27.6pc recorded in PP-203, according to Forms 47. The by-poll was held following the death of PML-N MPA Chaudhry Muhammad Hanif Jutt. This was the second time that a by-election was held in the constituency after the 2024 general elections. Notices were also issued to several PML-N lawmakers for alleged violations of the election code, mostly over visiting polling stations in the two constituencies. Earlier in the day, Chief Election Commissioner Sikander Sultan Raja visited the provincial election chief’s office, where he was briefed on the polling process in both constituencies, ECP said . After the balloting process concluded, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, whose PML-N is in power in the province, made multiple posts on X, claiming her party was in the lead in both NA-77 and PP-203 . In one post, CM Maryam wrote, “This electoral victory is no ordinary victory. It is a resounding public rebuke to conspiracy peddlers, hate mongers and those who refuse to read the writing on the wall.” She contended that the results portrayed that the “politics of delivery is far more enduring than the politics of hate and revenge”. “I am glad politics has returned to delivery and performance. Wake up and smell the coffee… or keep sleeping in denial!” the PML-N leader added. Notices over alleged electoral conduct violations While the polling was under way, notices, copies of which are available with Dawn , were issued to Punjab MPA Qudsia Batool, MNA Saira Afzal Tarar and Parliamentary Secretary for Information and Culture Shazia Rizwan for alleged violation of the Code of Conduct after reports emerged on social media that the three had visited various polling stations within NA-77, a statement issued by the office of the provincial election commissioner said. Notices were also issued over alleged violations of the Code of Conduct to PML-N’s MNA Syeda Nosheen Iftikhar and MPA Hina Arshad Warraich for allegedly visiting polling stations. The officials were directed to appear at the Election Complex in Gujranwala for an explanation at 3pm. Separately, PML-N leader and Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari claimed in a post on X that supporters of PMML candidate Qazi Ibrahim Gujjar were caught “openly stamping ballots” with the election commission staff present. Acting on the complaint, the provincial election commissioner said the returning officer concerned has been directed to probe the matter and submit a report. On Saturday, the ECP took notice of an alleged violation of the Code of Conduct by Information Minister Attaullah Tarar during by-election campaigning in NA-77 . According to a cause list issued on Sunday, Tarar, along with Virk, Batool and others, has been summoned to appear at the next hearing on Nov 12. According to the ECP, the minister visited the constituency by helicopter and addressed a campaign event for Rashid, violating a provision in the Code of Conduct , which bars public office holders from participating in campaign activities. ECP has sought a report from the district monitoring officer and the district returning officer to inquire into the matter. The watchdog also said that the result of the constituency could be withheld until a final decision is made on the matter. Meanwhile, notices were also issued to PML-N MPAs Malik Qasim Nadeem and Motiya Begum for allegedly visiting several polling stations in Chichawatni’s PP-203 on the polling day. The notices issued by the district monitoring officer, seen by Dawn , accused both of violating Para 48 of the Code of Conduct, which bars “all kinds of campaigns” and canvassing within a 400-metre radius of a polling station. The MPAs were asked to appear either in person or through counsel at the Municipal Committee Office at 5pm on Nov 9 (Monday) to clarify their position. Polling in PP-203 The seat was initially won in 2024 by independent candidate Rai Murtaza Iqbal, backed by the PTI, with 55,874 votes against Jutt, who polled 35,163 votes. However, Iqbal, along with four other PTI-backed parliamentarians, was disqualified and denotified by the ECP following their conviction by an anti-terrorism court in Faisalabad on July 31. Subsequently, the ECP scheduled a by-election for Nov 23, 2025, which was won by Jutt with 46,820 votes. His closest rival, independent candidate Falik Sher, secured 10,975 votes. Jutt died of cardiac arrest on Sept 17 this year, necessitating Sunday’s by-election in the constituency. Around 1,370 polling personnel, including 574 women and 796 men, were deputed at 185 polling stations across the constituency. District Police Officer Usman Tipu said 1,100 personnel had been deployed to ensure security during the by-election. A total of 185 polling stations had been established in the constituency, including 11 in Category A, 37 in Category B and 137 in Category C. A comprehensive traffic management plan had also been devised, with more than 65 personnel assigned duties.

items.title: 'Misplaced over-smartness': Maryam removes Jhelum DC over exam postponement for her visit
items.description: Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz removed the Jhelum deputy commissioner (DC) from his post on Sunday, after it emerged that computer science papers for intermediate students in the district had been postponed in the district owing to arrangements for the provincial chief executive’s scheduled visit on Nov 10. Originally scheduled for Nov 10, the computer science papers for the Intermediate Second Annual Examinations 2026 had been deferred on the recommendation of the now-dismissed Jhelum DC, Mir Raza Ozgen. He wrote in a letter to the Rawalpindi Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education (BISE) that due to the deployment of administrative and security personnel during the scheduled visit, “it is not feasible to ensure the smooth and uninterrupted conduct of the said examination in the district. It is, therefore, requested that the examination be postponed and rescheduled for another suitable date to avoid any inconvenience to students and ensure the smooth conduct of both the examination and the VVIP visit”. The move also came under scrutiny and criticism on social media. Eventually, Maryam posted on X that the Jhelum DC was being removed from his post with “immediate effect”. She said she had given “explicit instructions that no inconvenience or disruption whatsoever should be caused to the public during my visits to the districts”. “This is a clear disregard for my directions,” she added. Maryam also shared a second correspondence, dated Nov 6, by the then-Jhelum DC, who had advised the BISE chairperson to change one of the examination centres, Comprehensive Government School, in view of the “VVIP visit” and possible traffic congestion. In another post, she shared a notification that said the DC had been transferred and was instructed to report to the Punjab Services and General Administration Department for further orders. A later notification said Asma Ijaz, a BS-19 officer of the Pakistan Administrative Service (PAS), has been transferred and posted as the new Jhelum DC. Maryam also announced that the earlier postponed exams would now be held in line with the original schedule, on Nov 10. “Notwithstanding any acts of foolishness or misplaced over-smartness on part of the district administration, the examinations shall be held strictly in accordance with the original schedule, i.e. Tuesday, 10th November,” she posted on X. Subsequently, BISE withdrew its order to reschedule the exam via a notification, seen by Dawn . It stated that the examination would proceed as per its original schedule. In yet another X post, CM Maryam said she has directed all regional and district police officers as well as commissioners and deputy commissioners to ensure that “no market, shop, business, or any other establishment shall be closed or asked to suspend its operations on account of my visit.” She added that no residential streets will be blocked or sealed, or any restriction be placed on the movement of residents “under the pretext of security arrangements”. “Please ensure that all security measures are discreet and do not cause any inconvenience, disruption, or hardship to the general public,” she wrote, adding that the instructions must be “followed in letter and spirit”. “Failing to comply will result in strict action.” Additional input by Hamid Asghar

items.title: Turkiye's President Erdogan, Azerbaijan counterpart vow unity after tensions
items.description: Turkiye’s President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Azerbaijan’s President Ilham Aliyev vowed on Sunday that their countries’ alliance would remain solid, in a show of unity aimed at overcoming a public rift between the close neighbours. Tensions flared in September, when Baku revised school uniform regulations to prohibit clothing deemed incompatible with secular education, effectively barring Islamic headscarves in classrooms. Erdogan’s government has dismantled restrictions on hijabs in Turkiye. Azerbaijan’s move sparked protests at home and drew criticism from Erdogan’s Justice and Development Party (AKP). Presidential adviser Oktay Saral demanded that Azerbaijan reverse the restrictions. Aliyev’s ruling party, Yeni Azerbaijan, denounced the comments as “interference in Azerbaijan’s internal affairs”. Baku also declared 31 Turkish nationals, including an opposition lawmaker and party leaders, persona non grata over critical social media posts. Erdogan subsequently dismissed Saral, but Aliyev stayed away from an Oct 30 summit of Turkic leaders in Ankara — despite a personal invitation from Erdogan. Instead, he sent Foreign Minister Jeyhun Bayramov. On Sunday, as Azerbaijan marked Victory Day commemorating a 2020 war with Armenia, Erdogan arrived in the country’s Fuzuli district, which Baku recaptured from Armenian forces six years ago. A guard of honour lined up at the airport, where Aliyev and First Lady Mehriban Aliyeva welcomed Erdogan and his wife Emine. “With the permission of Almighty God, our unity will endure forever,” Erdogan told a joint press conference with Aliyev. “This unity of hearts, which we describe with the motto ‘One Nation, Two States,’ is an everlasting torch that draws strength from our shared past and illuminates our future.” Aliyev said the alliance — “an important factor across a vast geographical area” — remained unshaken. “Together, Azerbaijan and Turkiye are even stronger,” he said, adding that Erdogan’s visit “shows the whole world our unity”. “I am confident that this unity will last forever.” ‘Deeper rift’ Analysts say the quarrel reflects deeper unease over Baku’s diplomatic independence and its close ties to Israel. “Azerbaijan-Turkiye tensions stemmed from the fact that Baku does not see itself as the younger brother in this alliance and insists on relations between equal partners,” Elkhan Shahinoglu, head of the Baku-based Atlas Research Centre, told AFP . “The hijab dispute is a symptom of a deeper rift,” Gonul Tol, an analyst at the Washington-based Middle East Institute, wrote on X. “Tensions have long simmered over a number of issues including Azerbaijan’s sovereignty, Ankara’s influence in Baku, diverging policies toward Israel, and Turkiye’s rapprochement with Armenia.” Baku has forged strong military and economic ties with Israel, which supplied Azerbaijan with weapons during its 2020 war with Armenia over the breakaway Karabakh region. This angered Turkiye, which has grown increasingly hostile towards Israel over the Gaza conflict. Erdogan has accused Israel of genocide . Turkiye is also seeking to normalise relations with Armenia, whose border it closed in the 1990s in solidarity with Azerbaijan, while linking progress to Armenian-Azerbaijani peace efforts. Nov 8 marks Azerbaijan’s capture of the city of Shusha in Karabakh during its war with Armenia, a victory achieved with Turkish backing. The Turkic-speaking allies describe their relationship as “one nation, two states” and, despite the friction, remain closely bound by military and energy ties. Turkiye serves as a key transit route for Azerbaijani oil and gas exports to Western markets. An ex-Soviet republic, Azerbaijan is a mainly Shia Muslim country, but after decades of Soviet rule it emerged as one of the most secular states in the Muslim world.

items.title: Hamzat, GRV unveil contrasting plans at Lagos governorship debate
items.description: By Efe Onodjae Lagos State Deputy Governor and governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress, APC, Dr Obafemi Hamzat, and his African Democratic Congress, ADC, counterpart, have outlined contrasting development plans, with emphasis on housing, transportation, security, infrastructure and accountable governance. The candidates spoke at the 2026 Lagos State Governorship Debate, where they presented their credentials, policy proposals and vision for the state ahead of the governorship election. Hamzat, who described the debate as a job interview, said his experience in public service and previous appointments had prepared him for the responsibility of leading Lagos. He said: “I take tonight as a job interview. The first question you ask anybody that wants this type of responsibility is, what have you done to prepare for this job?” Recounting his professional background, Hamzat said he had worked as a teacher, case manager in New York and systems manager before joining public service. He said his experience as Commissioner for Science and Technology equipped him to oversee the development of the state’s residents and structural database, while his tenure as Commissioner for Works and Infrastructure saw him lead the team that delivered the decade-long bridge project, described as the first cable bridge in West Africa and second in Africa. According to him, effective governance requires a leader who understands the people, the state and the responsibilities of the office. On his governing philosophy, Hamzat identified respect for citizens, hard work and truthfulness as the principles that would guide his administration. He said government must place work before announcements and ensure transparency by telling citizens the truth about its activities. Unveiling his development blueprint, tagged Jacob’s Promise, Hamzat said it was built around seven pillars, seven broad areas of action and 100 pledges. He urged voters to assess candidates based on the substance of their plans and the work behind their promises rather than mere political announcements. Meanwhile, the Lagos ADC governorship candidate Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour said Lagos needed a departure from what he described as two decades of bad governance, insisting that the state must work for all residents rather than a privileged few. He said his political activism and manifesto had consistently prioritised the interests of ordinary people, adding that anyone seeking to govern a state with about 20 million residents must demonstrate a record of putting public interest above personal ambition. The ADC candidate said his administration would adopt an integrated approach to urban development, arguing that waste management, housing, transportation, healthcare, education and urban planning were interconnected. On housing, he promised to deliver 100,000 housing units within his first four years through a combination of luxury taxation to fund social housing, development of the eastern foreshore and intergenerational areas, and decentralisation of development across the state. He also proposed expanding rail infrastructure, promising to connect the state’s rail lines within two and a half years through a private-sector-driven approach that would be transparent, equitable and cost-effective. items.title: Le gouvernement adopte le projet de loi portant création de l’Institut national de sécurité sociale
items.description: Lomé, 7 nov. (ATOP)- Le conseil des ministres s’est réuni le vendredi 6 novembre, sous la présidence du Président du Conseil, Faure Gnassingbé pour adopter le projet de loi portant création de l’Institut national de sécurité sociale. Au cours des travaux, le conseil a adopté 1 projet de loi et 1 décret, examiné en première lecture 1 projet de loi et 1 projet de décret puis écouté trois communications. Adopt ion du projet de loi portant création de l’Institut national de sécurité sociale La couverture sociale des agents publics et assimilés est actuellement assurée par deux (2) organismes distincts à savoir : la Caisse de retraites du Togo (CRT), chargée de la gestion des pensions, et l’Institut national d’assurance maladie (INAM), chargé de l’assurance maladie. Cette organisation entraîne une multiplication des démarches pour les bénéficiaires, un dédoublement des structures et des charges de gestion, ainsi que des disparités dans la qualité des services. Afin de remédier à ces contraintes et de renforcer l’efficacité du système de protection sociale, le gouvernement a engagé une réforme visant à fusionner la CRT et l’INAM au sein d’un organisme unique dénommé Institut national de sécurité sociale (INSS). L’INSS sera chargé d’assurer la gestion des régimes de retraite et d’assurance maladie des agents publics et assimilés ainsi que de leurs ayants droit. Cette nouvelle organisation permettra notamment d’instaurer un guichet unique pour les assurés et de mutualiser les ressources, en vue d’améliorer la qualité des services offerts aux agents publics civils et militaires en activité, aux retraités et à leurs ayants droit, tout en renforçant l’efficacité et la pérennité du système de protection sociale. A travers cette réforme, précise le communiqué final des travaux, le gouvernement réaffirme sa volonté de bâtir un système de protection sociale plus intégré, équitable et durable, garantissant une meilleure prise en charge des agents publics et de leurs familles tout au long de leur parcours professionnel et après leur départ à la retraite. Le projet de loi modifiant la loi du 14 juin 2018 portant code foncier et domanial examiné en première lecture Adopté le 14 juin 2018, le Code foncier et domanial a constitué une étape importante dans la modernisation de la gouvernance foncière au Togo. Toutefois, sa mise en œuvre a révélé certaines insuffisances et difficultés d’application, ainsi que la nécessité d’adapter plusieurs de ses dispositions aux évolutions technologiques, sociales, économiques et environnementales. Le projet de loi examiné ce jour vise donc à améliorer ce cadre juridique, à travers l’introduction de plusieurs innovations portant notamment sur le renforcement de la gouvernance foncière, avec la création d’un Observatoire national du foncier, la modernisation de la gestion foncière par la numérisation et le recours aux technologies innovantes, la sécurisation des droits fonciers coutumiers et ruraux et la promotion de l’égalité entre les femmes et les hommes dans l’accès à la terre. Il prévoit également la protection des terres agricoles et des ressources naturelles, la prise en compte des enjeux pastoraux et climatiques, le renforcement de la procédure d’accès au foncier par les étrangers, la lutte contre la spéculation, la facilitation de l’accès des jeunes à la terre et au financement agricole, ainsi que l’amélioration du règlement des conflits fonciers et le renforcement des sanctions. Le gouvernement entend, à travers ce projet de loi, promouvoir un système foncier moderne, transparent, inclusif et sécurisé, garantissant une meilleure gestion du patrimoine foncier national et contribuant à la promotion de l’investissement et au développement durable. Le décret fixant les modalités d’application de la loi n° 2025-005 du 1er avril 2025 portant régime juridique applicable aux entreprises publiques adopté Dans le cadre de la modernisation de la gouvernance des entreprises publiques, le gouvernement a fait adopter, le 1er avril 2025, la loi n° 2025-005 qui a introduit plusieurs innovations visant notamment à renforcer le rôle des tutelles, à systématiser les contrats de performance entre l’Etat et les entreprises publiques, à promouvoir une administration indépendante et à clarifier les règles de fonctionnement de ces entreprises. Le décret adopté précise les modalités d’application de cette loi, notamment en matière d’exercice de la tutelle, de contrôle interne et externe, d’audit, de suivi et d’évaluation des contrats de performance, d’autorisation préalable de certains actes par le ministre chargé des finances, ainsi que de création et de fonctionnement des entreprises publiques des collectivités territoriales. Il encadre également les procédures de dissolution et de liquidation des entreprises publiques. Ce texte vise ainsi à assurer la mise en œuvre effective de la loi et à renforcer la transparence, la performance et la responsabilité dans la gestion des entreprises publiques. Le Conseil a ensuite examiné en première lecture un projet de décret portant création, attributions, organisation et fonctionnement de la commission nationale de lutte contre les activités minières illicites Ce projet de décret a pour objectif de renforcer la coordination des actions des administrations compétentes face à la recrudescence des activités minières illicites, notamment l’orpaillage clandestin et l’exploitation sans titre, dont les conséquences sont préoccupantes sur les plans environnemental, économique, sanitaire et sécuritaire. Une communication relative aux conclusions du premier séminaire national des gouverneurs et des préfets Tenu les 05 et 06 août 2026 à Blitta, sous le thème : « Renforcer le pilotage territorial de l’action de l’Etat : bilan du premier semestre 2026 et perspectives d’amélioration », ce séminaire a constitué un cadre d’échanges et de réflexion sur les conditions de renforcement de la gouvernance territoriale et de l’articulation entre les administrations centrales, les services déconcentrés et les autorités territoriales. Il a permis de dresser le bilan des actions menées par les autorités territoriales et de dégager des pistes d’amélioration, notamment en matière de collaboration administrative, de partage de l’information et de suivi des décisions et des projets publics. Dans cette perspective, plusieurs mesures ont été proposées en vue de renforcer la coordination de l’action de l’Etat dans les territoires. Elles portent notamment sur la clarification des modalités de collaboration entre les administrations publiques et les autorités territoriales, la généralisation des conférences administratives régionales et préfectorales à compter de janvier 2027, le renforcement des capacités des gouvernorats et des préfectures, ainsi que l’institutionnalisation du séminaire national. Le Président du Conseil a instruit le ministre de prendre les dispositions nécessaires à la mise en œuvre des mesures proposées, notamment l’institutionnalisation du séminaire national des gouverneurs et des préfets, et son élargissement à d’autres membres du gouvernement, afin de consolider le pilotage territorial de l’action gouvernementale, d’améliorer la coordination des interventions publiques et de renforcer le suivi des politiques publiques dans les régions et les préfectures. Une communication relative à l’adoption de la déclaration de politique du secteur postal Dans un contexte marqué par l’essor du numérique et du commerce électronique, le secteur postal constitue un levier important de développement économique et d’inclusion sociale. Toutefois, malgré son potentiel et la présence de plusieurs opérateurs, il reste confronté à des défis liés notamment à la transformation numérique, à l’accessibilité des services postaux, à la modernisation de la Société des postes du Togo et à l’adaptation du cadre réglementaire. Pour répondre à ces enjeux, une politique nationale de développement du secteur postal, pour la période 2026-2029 a été élaborée autour de la vision de faire du secteur postal un acteur majeur de l’économie numérique, de favoriser l’émergence d’un marché concurrentiel et dynamique et d’améliorer la performance du service postal universel. Cette politique repose sur cinq orientations stratégiques, à savoir la transformation digitale du secteur, le renforcement du cadre législatif et réglementaire, l’amélioration de la qualité et de l’accessibilité des services postaux, la promotion de l’inclusion financière à travers des services numériques innovants, ainsi que le développement du commerce électronique et des services logistiques. Le Conseil des ministres a autorisé la soumission de cette politique à son adoption, en vue de renforcer la compétitivité du secteur postal et sa contribution à la transformation numérique et au développement socioéconomique du Togo. Une communication relative au cadre général de la gestion des investissements publics au Togo Dans le cadre des réformes engagées pour améliorer la gestion des finances publiques, plusieurs évaluations du système de gestion des investissements publics ont mis en évidence la nécessité de renforcer le cadre réglementaire régissant la préparation, la sélection, la programmation, l’exécution et le suivi des projets d’investissement public. A cet effet, un projet de décret a été élaboré afin d’harmoniser et de formaliser les règles applicables à l’ensemble du cycle de vie des investissements publics, quels que soient les organismes concernés et les sources de financement. Ce projet de décret prévoit notamment le renforcement de l’alignement des projets sur les priorités nationales de développement, la systématisation de leur évaluation préalable, la clarification des rôles et responsabilités des acteurs, ainsi que la prise en compte des enjeux liés au genre, au climat et à la protection de l’environnement. Il prévoit également une meilleure anticipation des coûts récurrents, le renforcement du suivi physique et financier des projets et l’institutionnalisation des évaluations à mi-parcours, finales et ex post, ainsi que des audits externes. Cette réforme vise à améliorer la qualité de la dépense publique, à renforcer la transparence et la soutenabilité des investissements et à garantir une meilleure efficacité des projets réalisés au bénéfice des populations. Le Conseil a instruit les ministres concernés de poursuivre le processus en vue de lui soumettre, dans les meilleurs délais, le projet de décret pour adoption. ATOP/AJA/Communiqué du conseil des ministres

items.title: KNUST student dies after diving from 17.6-foot platform into swimming pool
items.description: A student of the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) in Kumasi has died after diving from a 17.6-foot-high platform into a swimming pool on campus. The deceased, identified as David Osei Oppong, was said to have gone swimming with some friends when he attempted a dive from the highest platform at the university’s swimming pool. In a short video circulating on social media, the Level 300 chemical engineering student is seen jumping from the platform and plunging into the water. However, a few seconds after entering the pool, David reportedly failed to resurface, prompting an emergency rescue effort by other swimmers and bystanders. Pool attendants at the facility immediately rushed to his aid and pulled him out of the water. Despite attempts to revive him through cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), he could not be saved. He was rushed to the university hospital for emergency medical care but couldn’t be saved. The incident reportedly occurred around 5 pm on Saturday, November 7, 2026. In a statement, the university mourned the loss of the student and said police have begun investigations into the circumstances leading to the student’s death. According to the university, Mr Agyapong was an experienced swimmer, a regular user of the swimming facility and a member of the university’s basketball team. His body has since been deposited at the morgue of the School of Medical Sciences at the University for autopsy. A video showing David Osei jumping from the 17.6ft platform before drowning to death. items.title: With Stephen Miller at the helm, Trump charts a course for confrontation
items.description: US President Donald Trump’s decision to elevate loyalist Stephen Miller to run his White House indicates that he plans to ramp up confrontation in his final two years in office and block outside political and economic pressures, Trump administration officials and other Republicans say. Voters delivered a historic rebuke to Republicans in Tuesday’s midterm election , but with Miller as White House chief of staff, the Trump administration is expected to continue its aggressive immigration crackdown , amplify cultural conflicts and give no ground to a Democratic-controlled Congress, say officials and experts who spoke to Reuters . They say wavering Republicans will face increased pressure to stay in line, while businesses may have a harder time making their case to the White House. “This signals the administration is going to have a fighting-from-a-bunker approach the last two years,” said Dan Eberhart, a Trump donor and energy executive. Although Trump has said he can work with Democrats, he has shown a feisty approach since the midterm election results became clear . On Saturday, he ordered the Justice Department to “look into” Democrats whom he accused of sending “threatening letters” to Republican donors and other Trump allies. The president also offered the job of White House press secretary to combat sports promoter Dana White. ‘This man saved America’ Miller, 41, marks a sharp contrast with outgoing chief of staff Susie Wiles , a former lobbyist who ran Trump’s 2024 presidential campaign . Wiles lacked significant Washington experience but was seen as a deft manager of competing interests. Miller, by contrast, is regarded by allies and foes alike as a combative ideologue with a deep knowledge of the levers of power and an unswerving loyalty to Trump. “If it wasn’t for President Trump, the United States of America would not exist right now. This man saved America,” Miller said at an event at Trump’s Florida estate on Friday. Miller joined Trump’s first presidential campaign in 2016 and served throughout his two terms in the White House. He is best known for driving Trump’s aggressive immigration crackdown , which has galvanised Trump’s supporters but alienated many voters. Only 37 per cent approve of Trump’s handling of immigration, according to an October Reuters /Ipsos poll, down from 50pc when he took office. Still, four US immigration officials told Reuters that there have been no signs that the administration will let up. “Nothing is changing, same quotas,” said one official, who spoke on condition of anonymity. Representative Don Bacon of Nebraska, an occasional Trump critic who is retiring, told Reuters that Miller “was in denial” as he and other Republican lawmakers tried to warn him before the election that Trump’s immigration and tariff policies were driving away voters. “We said, ‘You’re going to give us a bad midterm election,’ and he rejected it,” Bacon said. ‘Doubling down on a failed strategy’ The White House said Miller will continue to deliver “historic successes” in his new role, but Bacon said most of his peers in the House view it as “doubling down on a failed strategy”. “It’s going over like a lead balloon in most of Congress,” Bacon said of Miller’s appointment. Miller has also overseen Trump’s executive orders, giving him an expansive understanding of the administrative tools available to the president. Several people interviewed for this story said they expect the White House to rely on executive orders more extensively rather than working with lawmakers. Republican legislators will face pressure to stick with Trump through Democratic-led investigations to come, even if they damage the party as a whole. “Those on Capitol Hill looking to break away from the Trump administration will know that Stephen Miller is not going to sit idly by and watch that happen,“ said Republican strategist Ron Bonjean. Ending the Mideast war? As well as the domestic issues he has focused on for most of his career, Miller now will have a greater say in foreign affairs. Miller opposes prolonging the war with Iran , according to three sources familiar with his thinking who spoke on condition of anonymity, but he strongly supports Israel — potentially putting him at odds with a president who has threatened to resume strikes on Iran and announced he will end aid to Jerusalem. Miller’s elevation also has unnerved some corporate lobbyists, who worry he will not be as responsive to their issues as Wiles, who cultivated relationships with top executives. “This will be a big change,” said a senior lobbyist at a Trump-aligned firm who spoke on condition of anonymity. “Miller is there to focus on political priorities, like immigration and tariffs , stuff Trump cares about, and won’t have the same approach as Susie, who understood policies have unintended consequences.” Miller’s appointment was met with praise from senior cabinet officials and political supporters, who described him as the fighter they will need in Trump’s final stretch. “I think Donald Trump has found his wartime consigliere,” Trump ally Roger Stone told Reuters .

items.title: ANC suffers worst-ever election result in South Africa
items.description: The African National Congress (ANC), which has dominated South African politics since the end of apartheid, has recorded its worst-ever electoral performance, securing 30.76 per cent of the votes in municipal elections, according to the country’s electoral commission. The final results, announced on Sunday, showed that the party’s support had declined further, setting the stage for difficult multiparty coalition negotiations in several major cities where no party secured an outright majority. The liberal Democratic Alliance (DA), the ANC’s closest challenger and main partner in the national unity government, secured about a quarter of the votes, according to the final tally. Chairperson of the Electoral Commission of South Africa, Mosotho Moepya, said voter turnout stood at 52 per cent, six percentage points higher than the 2021 municipal elections, which were affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. Moepya also disclosed that voting would be repeated in one municipality after party supporters stormed a polling station and destroyed ballot papers. The outcome represents a significant decline for the party of late liberation icon Nelson Mandela, which won nearly two-thirds of the votes in South Africa’s first democratic elections in 1994. Although the ANC remains the country’s largest political party, its support has steadily declined amid widespread unemployment, which has exceeded 34 per cent, as well as crime and corruption scandals. Water shortages, electricity outages and poor service delivery were among the major issues that shaped Wednesday’s elections as voters assessed the performance of parties governing their communities. Describing the outcome as “catastrophic”, ANC Secretary-General, Fikile Mbalula, acknowledged the party’s shortcomings on Saturday. “Where we have fallen short, this movement does not dispute it. Communities have gone without water. Refuse has not been collected. Roads have not been maintained,” he said. “We have been weighed in the balance, and where we have been found wanting we dare not quarrel with the scale,” Mbalula told reporters. More than half of South Africa’s 213 municipal councils failed to produce an outright majority for any party, making coalition arrangements necessary for the formation of local governments. Previous coalitions in the country have often been characterised by internal disagreements and shifting political alliances, resulting in administrative instability and disruptions to basic services. President Cyril Ramaphosa urged political parties to prioritise the interests of communities in their coalition negotiations, warning against allowing political disagreements to disrupt essential services. “The people have spoken. Their verdict must be respected. Their concerns must be heard and their expectations must now be met,” he said on Sunday. The parties face a tight timetable, as newly elected councils are legally required to hold their inaugural meetings within 14 days of the formal declaration of results to elect mayors and other office-holders. All but one of South Africa’s eight major cities require coalition negotiations, with the DA securing an outright majority in Cape Town. The DA was also leading in Johannesburg, the country’s economic hub, where it fielded 75-year-old veteran politician Helen Zille, a longtime critic of the ANC who previously built her political career in Cape Town. Meanwhile, centre-right ActionSA, founded by former Johannesburg mayor Herman Mashaba after his departure from the DA, finished fifth nationally but could play a decisive role in coalition negotiations in major metropolitan areas, including Tshwane, which is home to the administrative capital, Pretoria. items.title: Festival Zamane 2026 : l’Ahidous au cœur d’une célébration du patrimoine à M’Hamid El Ghizlane
items.description: Du 3 au 6 décembre 2026, M’Hamid El Ghizlane accueillera la cinquième édition du Festival Zamane, placée cette année sous le signe de l’Ahidous. Pendant quatre jours, plus de 150 musiciens mettront à l’honneur ce patrimoine musical amazigh, dans un rendez-vous qui entend conjuguer transmission culturelle, création artistique et préservation des oasis. Aux portes du Sahara, dans la vallée du Drâa, le Festival Zamane poursuit son travail de valorisation des traditions musicales du sud marocain. Organisée par l’association Joudour Sahara, fondée par Halim Sbai, cette cinquième édition consacrera une place centrale à l’Ahidous, pratique musicale et chorégraphique associant chants, rythmes, danses et poésie. Au-delà du spectacle, le festival entend mettre en lumière la transmission d’un patrimoine essentiellement oral. Plus de 150 musiciens d’Ahidous sont ainsi attendus à M’Hamid El Ghizlane, pour une célébration réunissant artistes, musiciens traditionnels, jeunes talents et communautés locales. À travers cette programmation, Joudour Sahara souhaite contribuer à préserver des traditions dont la transmission peut se fragiliser avec le temps. Depuis sa création en 2016, l’association travaille à documenter et valoriser les expressions musicales de la vallée du Drâa, notamment l’Ahidous, le Ganga, la Chamra et la Rokba. Le projet repose également sur la transmission intergénérationnelle. Des musiciens traditionnels accompagnent notamment les jeunes dans l’apprentissage des chants, des rythmes, des danses et des techniques liées à la fabrication des instruments. Cette démarche concerne aujourd’hui plus de 500 musiciens et jeunes, une vingtaine de communautés et un réseau de membres implanté dans la province de Zagora. Une scène ouverte aux artistes marocains et internationaux Zamane 2026 proposera également une programmation qui cherche à créer un dialogue entre musiques traditionnelles et expressions contemporaines. Parmi les artistes annoncés figurent Oum, Bassekou Kouyaté & Amy Sacko, Daraa Tribes, Feelin's 9 & Ahidous Tifsa et Saad Tiouly. Le festival accueillera également Roberto Luti, Julian Belbachir, Said Taragalte, Alberto Visentin, ainsi que le projet Nour Joudour, réunissant des artistes de France, du Maroc et d’Algérie. Cette dimension internationale doit permettre de multiplier les rencontres et les collaborations, tout en donnant une visibilité accrue aux traditions musicales du sud marocain. L’édition 2026 sera également marquée par l’ouverture officielle, le 3 décembre, du Centre Culturel Joudour Sahara à M’Hamid El Ghizlane. Développé avec Aziza Chaouni Projects, ce nouvel espace comprendra notamment un auditorium, un studio d’enregistrement, un réservoir d’eau et un espace d’accueil. Il doit permettre à l’association de poursuivre ses activités de création, de transmission et d’éducation musicale tout au long de l’année. Pour Joudour Sahara, l’enjeu est ainsi de dépasser le cadre d’un événement ponctuel et de créer une infrastructure permanente au service des artistes, des jeunes et des communautés locales. Quand la préservation du patrimoine passe aussi par celle des oasis À M’Hamid El Ghizlane, la question culturelle reste étroitement liée à celle de l’environnement. La raréfaction de l’eau, l’avancée des dunes et la dégradation des terres fragilisent les écosystèmes oasiens et les modes de vie qui leur sont associés. Le Festival Zamane intégrera donc une dimension environnementale à sa programmation. Plus de 200 arbres seront plantés dans la région avec la participation d’artistes, de jeunes, d’habitants et de festivaliers. L’initiative sera menée avec la Fondation Sahara Roots et s’appuiera sur la solution Groasis Waterbox, destinée à optimiser l’utilisation de l’eau dans les environnements arides. Conférences et débats consacrés à l’Ahidous, à son rôle dans la société contemporaine et aux enjeux environnementaux viendront compléter la programmation musicale. Les coopératives féminines de la région seront également associées au festival à travers la présentation de leurs créations artisanales et de leurs savoir-faire. items.title: Man United stage late comeback to snatch 4-4 draw against Aston Villa
items.description: Manchester United twice came from two goals down to salvage a remarkable 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday and potentially save manager Michael Carrick’s job. Goals in stoppage time from Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu rescued a point, but United will spend a two-week international break in the relegation zone. Carrick’s men conceded twice inside the opening four minutes as Alysson and Nicolas Jackson punished errors from goalkeeper Senne Lammens. The Red Devils rallied to level at half-time thanks to a Bruno Fernandes penalty and Youri Tielemans’s first goal since moving to Old Trafford from Villa. A thrilling fightback from 2-0 down to beat Roma 3-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday gave Carrick a lifeline. This time the comeback fell short as more woeful defending handed Villa two more goals inside the first eight minutes of the second period. John McGinn converted from the spot after Diogo Dalot upended Alysson before Leon Goretzka bundled in from close range. Yet, there was a final twist in the tale as Zirkzee steered home before Dorgu pounced when Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki failed to connect with a corner in the 96th minute. – ‘We want new owners’ – Carrick was handed a stay of execution after a 3-0 home drubbing by Bournemouth a fortnight ago. However, he faces an anxious wait to see if the United board install a replacement before a daunting trip to Liverpool on November 22. Former Newcastle United boss Eddie Howe and ex-Bayern Munich and Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann are among the leading contenders to take charge if Carrick is dismissed. Saturday’s results saw United slip into the relegation zone after August for the first time in 40 years. A draw keeps them in the bottom three with just eight points from 10 games. For the first time in Premier League history they found themselves 2-0 down inside four minutes, in large part due to goalkeeper Lammens. The Belgian allowed Alysson’s strike to slip between his legs with just one minute on the clock. From another tame Alysson effort less than three minutes later, Lammens could only parry and present Nicolas Jackson with a gift for his sixth goal in his last six league games. The United fans had again turned their ire towards the club’s owners pre-match. A banner read: “We don’t want a new stadium, we want new owners,” as protests towards a move away from Old Trafford gather steam. That anger was directed towards the players in cries of “you’re not fit to wear the shirt” in the wake of the second Villa goal. Yet, the shock of going behind summoned a response as United again found their feet at 2-0 down. Just as against Roma, the fightback was started by Matheus Cunha winning a penalty, converted by Fernandes. Boubacar Kamara dived in rashly to clip Cunha before getting a touch on the ball and Fernandes coolly sat down Suzuki to slot home the spot-kick. United built momentum before levelling just before the break when Tielemans drilled low beyond Suzuki, with the aid of a deflection. What should have been the launching pad for another stirring fightback quickly fell flat at the start of the second half. Dalot dived in foolishly to trip Alysson and McGinn made amends for missing from the spot in last weekend’s 1-1 draw against Fulham. Moments later Leny Yoro headed a McGinn free-kick off his own crossbar and Goretzka forced the ball over the line in the goalmouth scramble that ensued. The closing stages were played out to the tune of more protests against United’s unpopular American owners, the Glazer family, until the home side hauled themselves off the canvas again. Zirkzee’s cool finish reawakened the crowd and left Villa clinging on. Much to the frustration of Unai Emery, his side could not resist the late assault as Suzuki flapped at Fernandes’s corner and Dorgu accepted the gift. items.title: Europe : les géants de l'IA face à une vague de protestations contre leurs centres de données
items.description: Plus de 100 associations se sont retrouvees autour d'un meme mot d'ordre, « Stop Dirty Data Centres ». Les 6 et 7 novembre, la campagne s'est traduite par des actions dans une quinzaine de pays europeens. Les collectifs veulent faire suspendre les grands chantiers, le temps d'examiner leur impact sur la vie des habitants. Dans ces centres, des rangees de serveurs font fonctionner les services numeriques, dont ceux utilisant l'intelligence artificielle (IA). Ils degagent beaucoup de chaleur et doivent etre refroidis, parfois avec de l'eau. Les riverains redoutent des factures d'electricite plus lourdes et la disparition de terrains agricoles. Un chantier Microsoft occupe a Amsterdam, aux Pays-Bas, la mobilisation a pris un tour plus tendu. Le 6 novembre, des militants ont penetre sur le chantier d'un centre destine a Microsoft, groupe americain de logiciels et de services numeriques. Certains ont grimpe sur une grue, tandis que des fumigenes etaient allumes. L'Associated Press fait etat de 150 a 200 interpellations. Approximately 500 protesters broke into the construction site of a #Microsoft data center in the port area on the west side of #Amsterdam , reports AT5 television channel. https://t.co/1yj5IZgi11 — Mina (@Mina696645851) November 6, 2026 Cette occupation etait menee par un collectif local, distinct de la coalition europeenne qui manifestait aussi devant le site. La contestation a egalement gagne Varsovie et les environs de Berlin. En Irlande, quelque 2 000 personnes ont manifeste a Dublin le 7 novembre. En Finlande, environ 1 300 se sont rassemblees a Helsinki, d'apres les medias locaux cites par Bloomberg. La France aussi concernee En France, plusieurs projets cristallisent les critiques. a Fouju, en region parisienne, un ensemble de 11 centres de donnees est envisage sur 90 hectares de terres agricoles, selon le collectif Stop Campus IA. Une reunion publique y etait annoncee le 6 novembre. a Vitry-sur-Seine, pres de Paris, une visite du site des Ardoines figurait au programme des opposants. Le debat a deja gagne le Parlement francais. Le 8 octobre, le depute Francois Ruffin denoncait le developpement de ces infrastructures sans veritable choix public. « a quel moment, dans cette Assemblee, a ete pose le choix de faire des data centers une priorite dans notre pays ? Jamais ! », a-t-il declare. Des milliards malgre la contestation Les chantiers continuent pourtant d'attirer les investisseurs. D'apres une estimation de PwC, jusqu'a 176 milliards d'euros pourraient etre consacres aux centres de donnees en Europe entre 2026 et 2031. Bruxelles entend renforcer ses capacites informatiques face aux etats-Unis et a la Chine. Les collectifs veulent suspendre les autorisations de nouveaux grands chantiers pour en mesurer les effets avant toute construction. Ils ne demandent pas de fermer les centres deja ouverts. Leur mobilisation met en cause une course technologique soutenue par les autorites, dont les coûts en eau, en energie et en terres seraient supportes avant tout par les territoires concernes.
