items.title: MMFL selects five teams for Fintech Lab finals
items.description: MobileMoney Fintech LTD (MMFL) has selected five teams from the Accra Zonal Hackathon Pitch Competition of the 2026 MoMo Fintech Lab to advance to the National Mentorship Programme. The selection is part of the company’s efforts to nurture commercially viable financial technology solutions in Ghana. The Accra competition, held as part of the Southern Sector MMFL Fintech Lab Hackathon, brought together developers, entrepreneurs and startups to present technology-based solutions to everyday challenges. Speaking at the event, the Chief Products and Services Officer of MMFL, Sylvia Otu Achempong, said the journey began a few weeks ago with the launch of a technology-based competition for developers, entrepreneurs, and startups, creating a platform to bring the ecosystem together, involving banks, fintech companies, the central bank, and other partners. ”Following the competitions, MMFL began the zonal competitions, giving participants the opportunity to present their ideas and demonstrate how technology could address everyday challenges. The competition started in Tamale, where 12 participants presented their ideas, and five were selected to advance. As the competition progressed across the zones, organisers continued to see promising ideas and considerable enthusiasm from participants. During the Accra hackathon, Mrs Acheampong served as a judge and also delivered the keynote address on behalf of the leadership of MMFL. We heard 10 presentations covering areas such as small business support, savings, spending, and waste management, with mobile money serving as a platform for these solutions,” she said. Five outstanding teams emerged, each proposing a solution to a pressing problem. The winning solution addresses language barriers in digital financial services. Mrs Achempong explained that not everyone can read or easily understand the text-based interfaces used in digital financial services. “The team developed a model that allows users to interact with services through voice in multiple languages, helping to make those services more accessible,” she said. She commended the partners who have devoted their time and expertise to coaching the participants and helping them refine their ideas. Throughout this journey, our partners have devoted their time and expertise to coaching the participants and helping them refine their ideas, she noted. According to her, the next step is to help the ideas develop into viable businesses. “Our next step is to help these ideas develop into viable businesses. We want this platform to produce startups and solutions that can grow and serve customers,” she said. To achieve this, MMFL will continue to provide technical support and help participants strengthen their business skills. Mrs Acheampong said participants would also be encouraged to test their solutions with customers, gather feedback and use those insights to improve their products. “We hope that all 15 contestants emerging from the zonal competitions will return with stronger, more developed solutions,” she said. Bringing a competition of that scale together, she said, requires considerable effort, but the response has shown the value of continuing and expanding it.“We will challenge ourselves to do more, broaden participation and encourage more people to develop the confidence to put their ideas forward,” she said. She disclosed that this year, MMFL received 1,791 applications for the competition — the highest number recorded since it began running competitions of that kind.

items.title: Trump says he is unlikely to order Iran attack if talks progress, CNN reports
items.description: Nov 8 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump on Sunday said he was highly unlikely to order fresh attacks on Iran as long as talks to end the conflict progress, CNN reported. "It depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement," CNN cited Trump as saying in a phone interview. "The answer is, highly unlikely it's going to be necessary." CNN did not specify exactly what it had asked Trump, who also said the US had identified potential infrastructure targets. These included 38 bridges "that we can knock down in literally one hour," he said.

items.title: Eisenkot says Israel in 'devastating diplomatic crisis' as he seeks to form govt
items.description: Israel’s former military chief Gadi Eisenkot started the tough task on Sunday of forming a government, reaching out to Benjamin Netanyahu’s allies as he warned the veteran prime minister had brought the country to a historic crisis. Eisenkot, 66, a political novice who has vowed to bridge Israel’s deep polarisation under Netanyahu, formally received a mandate from President Isaac Herzog, giving him 28 days to form a government despite his bloc lacking a clear majority. “We are in a state of emergency, approaching a point of no return for the State of Israel,” Eisenkot said at a ceremony at the presidential office. Both Eisenkot and Herzog acknowledged Israel’s growing isolation under Netanyahu, who is wanted by the International Criminal Court over allegations of crimes against humanity and war crimes in Gaza. “We are in the midst of a devastating diplomatic crisis. Even our closest friends and strategic allies are saying their relationship with Israel must be reassessed,” Eisenkot said. “We must form a national emergency government. This will require creative and unconventional political steps,” Eisenkot stressed. He said Israeli democracy was at a vulnerable moment at a time when it faced immense challenges. “There is great urgency for new leadership, leadership that people can look in the eye and trust,” he said. Eisenkot appealed to Netanyahu’s Likud Party as well as the far-right party of Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich to join — but only with himself as prime minister. “My door is open and my hand is extended, wholeheartedly and willingly, to anyone who understands the gravity of this moment,” he said. Meanwhile, Herzog cited a threat of attack from Iran, the need to progress towards peace in Gaza and negotiations with Lebanon and other neighbours. “We need to start shaping the political horizon in the region, and we also have to present the 20 points of the agreement in the Gaza strip, and consultations with our neighbours in Lebanon and the region,” he was quoted as saying in a translation by Al Jazeera . “We also have to deal with the sanctions and the political challenges in light of the recent political developments in the United States,” the Israeli president said. In the United States, the most vital ally of Israel, Democrats on Tuesday swept the midterm elections with calls to rein in Israel after the devastation in Gaza and the unpopular Iran war which Netanyahu launched with President Donald Trump. Eisenkot, born to a family of working-class Moroccan immigrants, would be the first Sephardic prime minister — a community mostly descended from Middle Eastern or North African Jews — in a country long dominated by an Ashkenazi elite with ties to Europe. Netanyahu is Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, having led the country on and off for nearly two decades. He has taken the country in a sharply rightward direction and led wars against Gaza, Lebanon and Iran since the Oct 7, 2023 attacks by Hamas. Netanyahu called for a unity government of all Zionist parties to preserve a Jewish state, while giving no indication whether he was prepared to serve under Eisekenkot’s leadership. “This is the will of the people and the need of the hour,” he said in a statement, ruling out a coalition government with Arabs — who make up 21 per cent of Israel’s population. Nearly all Jewish parties now share Netanyahu’s rejection of an eventual independent Palestinian state, the basis of internationally endorsed peace efforts since the 1990s. Negotiations can take 6 weeks Eisenkot’s potential pathways to power include trying to form a minority government with Arab party support for key issues; forming a coalition with ultra-Orthodox parties that he and his allies have shunned in the past; or forging a unity government with Netanyahu. All three options face formidable obstacles. Eisenkot has appeared to suggest he is willing to start off with a minority government — relying on outside votes from Arab-Israeli parties — before bringing other lawmakers into his coalition. He said he will call on all parties to join who meet his main principles. These include recognition of Israel as a Jewish and democratic state; a duty of national service for all to strengthen the military and expand its ranks; and recognition of Hamas as a terrorist organisation and a commitment to destroying its military and governing capacity. “I am convinced that it is possible and right to form a new government quickly, one that will win a large majority in the Knesset,” Eisenkot said, referring to Israel’s parliament. Eisenkot now has 28 days plus a possible 14-day extension. If he fails, Netanyahu will likely get his shot at forming a government. Should he also be unable, new elections could be called. Assaf Shapira, a political expert at the Israel Democracy Institute, said Eisenkot would face an exceptionally fragile government if it only had 48 lawmakers in the 120-member parliament, with extensive negotiations needed on every piece of legislation. Eisenkot’s views Eisenkot has vowed to put an end to rampant violence against Palestinians by extremist West Bank settlers supported by Netanyahu’s government and has warned that the incumbent premier does not have the mandate for another attack on Iran. But he shares Netanyahu’s hawkish security views that have hardened since Oct 7, 2023: he opposes Palestinian statehood and says Hamas’s military wing must be destroyed or dismantled. He emphasised his security credentials on the campaign trail, citing his “ Dahiya doctrine ” of responding to attacks with disproportionate force, which he deployed as a commander during Israel’s 2006 war with Hezbollah in Lebanon. Both Eisenkot and Netanyahu say Israeli troops will not withdraw from Gaza until Hamas ​is disarmed, and that Israel is prepared to ​restart fighting to achieve this. Although Eisenkot has criticised settler violence against Palestinians in occupied West Bank, which has surged since 2023, he favours settlement in principle and says it should comply with Israeli law. He opposes settlements built without authorisation, aims to dismantle outposts in areas where ​they are forbidden and has pledged to rein in violent settlers. Wooing the ultra-Orthodox In consultations last week with Herzog, Eisenkot received recommendations from parties accounting for 67 lawmakers, against 46 for Netanyahu. But that vote count included Israeli Arabs, whose seat haul surged to a historic high on anger over Netanyahu’s government and whom several parties oppose having in government. Potentially making Eisenkot’s job tougher is the position of one opposition leader, Avigdor Lieberman of the Israel Our Home party, who has ruled out a unity government with Netanyahu or a minority government that has backing from Arab parties. Lieberman, a former Netanyahu aide turned sharp critic who nonetheless shares his hawkish views, has been adamant against any alliance with Arab Israelis, who are descendants of Palestinians who stayed after Israel’s creation in 1948. But Lieberman has softened his stance on sitting with ultra-Orthodox Jewish parties as long as they agree to support a law under which ultra-Orthodox men serve in the military. Taking back one of his signature campaign pledges, Lieberman instead voiced an openness to an alliance with ultra-Orthodox Jews, whose almost singular priority is ensuring that they remain exempt from military service. The exemption for the ultra-Orthodox — whose two main parties had been aligned with Netanyahu but could push Eisenkot to a majority — has been a source of growing resentment for many Israelis as reservists fight on multiple tours of duty. Lieberman said on Sunday he still backed conscription for all Israelis but that he had to make “difficult decisions” for the higher priority of ousting Netanyahu, who faces corruption charges that could land him in jail if he loses power. Naftali Bennett, the second strongest opposition leader after Lieberman, has also been outspoken against the ultra-Orthodox community’s military exemption and has stayed quiet since Lieberman’s about-face. In Tel Aviv, Neri Bar-On, who works in educational technology, said he expected Eisenkot to succeed in forming a government. “But the problems run deeper,” he said. “The country is facing a massive internal conflict; even if he manages to form a government, it won’t solve the underlying issues.”

items.title: We are united and ready to fight for Africa’s interests at COP31 – AGN Chair
items.description: Nearly 200 countries are converging on Antalya, Türkiye, from November 9 to 20 to advance the implementation of the Paris Agreement on climate change, amid mounting pressure on world leaders to ensure that climate finance reaches communities hardest hit by climate change. The UN Climate Change Conference (COP31), dubbed the “implementation COP,” will focus on translating existing commitments and pledges into tangible climate action to unlock greater resilience, improve health outcomes and create economic opportunities for people. The African Group of Negotiators on Climate Change (AGN) has spent the past week in Antalya coordinating and aligning the continent’s priorities ahead of the negotiations. The preparations have included consultations with UN Climate Change Executive Secretary Simon Stiell and the Chairs of both UNFCCC Subsidiary Bodies, providing opportunities to engage on Africa’s priorities ahead of the conference. The Group’s Chair, Nana Dr Antwi-Boasiako Amoah, has acknowledged that securing agreement on the agenda when the conference opens on Monday will not be easy. However, he says Africa is seeking cooperation to ensure that its proposed agenda items are considered and that the necessary finance is made available for implementation. Africa is particularly pushing for a tripling of adaptation finance and the replenishment of the Green Climate Fund. “The agenda items that we have proposed are very important for the survival of our people within the continent, and there is no way we’re going to compromise on them,” said the Chair. Nana Amoah has emphasised the need for “one Africa, a united voice and a shared ambition for development” in the climate process, as the continent seeks to advance outcomes that respond to its development aspirations. “We will firmly defend the agenda items we have proposed and work for outcomes that respond to our people’s needs, protect our development aspirations and deliver on climate commitments. Africa’s voice must count, and our priorities must shape the decisions,” Nana Dr Antwi-Boasiako Amoah stated. The AGN is advocating climate action that supports resilient economies, improves livelihoods and promotes sustainable development, backed by the necessary finance, technology and capacity to deliver meaningful results. Delegates from across the world are arriving in Antalya, representing national negotiating teams, youth groups, Indigenous Peoples, scientists, civil society organisations and the media.

items.title: Fonction publique : les femmes dominent dans la santé et la justice, mais restent minoritaires dans l’emploi
items.description: La fonction publique marocaine continue de se féminiser, mais cette progression ne suffit pas à compenser les difficultés persistantes des femmes sur le marché du travail. Alors que leur présence s’affirme dans certains secteurs de l’administration, notamment la santé et la justice, leur accès à l’emploi, particulièrement dans le secteur privé, demeure limité. Les dernières données officielles mettent également en évidence les obstacles qui subsistent en matière d’accès aux postes de décision. Selon le rapport sur les ressources humaines annexé au projet de loi de finances, les femmes représentent désormais 68 % des fonctionnaires du secteur public de la santé. Elles sont également majoritaires dans la justice, où leur part atteint 51,9 % des effectifs. Ces deux secteurs figurent ainsi parmi les administrations les plus féminisées du pays. Dans d’autres départements, la représentation féminine se rapproche progressivement de celle des hommes, sans toutefois atteindre la parité. Les femmes constituent 41,8 % des effectifs de l’éducation nationale, 41,4 % de ceux de l’économie et des finances et 38,3 % de ceux de l’enseignement supérieur. Cette présence reste néanmoins concentrée dans un nombre limité de départements ministériels. Le rapport indique que 87,8 % des fonctionnaires femmes travaillent dans six secteurs : l’éducation nationale, la santé, l’intérieur, la justice, l’enseignement supérieur et l’économie et les finances. À elles seules, l’éducation nationale, la santé et l’enseignement supérieur regroupent 69,7 % de l’ensemble des fonctionnaires femmes. Ces trois secteurs représentent respectivement 41,3 %, 22,8 % et 5,6 % de leurs effectifs. Une féminisation qui ne masque pas les inégalités Malgré ces avancées, l’analyse de la structure des effectifs des fonctionnaires civils de l’État en 2026, selon le genre, révèle des disparités persistantes dans la répartition des ressources humaines au sein de la fonction publique. « Malgré les acquis et les efforts déployés par le gouvernement, avec le soutien des organismes des Nations unies, l’intégration des femmes dans le marché du travail et leur accès aux postes de décision demeurent parmi les principaux défis », souligne le document. Le taux global de féminisation de la fonction publique s’établit à 35,7 %, un niveau qui reste relativement limité au regard de la représentation masculine. Pour renforcer l’égalité entre les femmes et les hommes, le Maroc s’est doté de plusieurs dispositifs institutionnels. La Constitution de 2011 consacre ce principe et prévoit la création d’une instance chargée de la parité et de la lutte contre toutes les formes de discrimination. Le Royaume a également lancé, en partenariat avec les Nations unies, le Programme national intégré d’autonomisation économique et sociale des femmes. Celui-ci vise à renforcer leur autonomie, à réduire les inégalités et à favoriser leur participation dans les différents domaines de la vie économique et sociale. Le rapport rappelle également l’engagement du Maroc en faveur de l’égalité et des droits des femmes à travers la ratification de plusieurs conventions internationales relatives aux droits humains, notamment la Convention des Nations unies sur l’élimination de toutes les formes de discrimination à l’égard des femmes. Dans le prolongement de ces engagements, le pays a adopté une approche budgétaire sensible au genre, destinée à orienter les politiques publiques et les programmes vers la promotion de l’égalité et à garantir une répartition équitable des ressources financières. Le taux d’emploi féminin recule par rapport à 2000 Ces dispositifs institutionnels se heurtent toutefois à une réalité persistante : la faible participation des femmes au marché du travail. Selon les données du rapport sur le genre, le taux d’emploi des femmes, tous secteurs confondus, ne dépassait pas 15,1 % en 2025, contre 24,5 % en 2000. Ce recul souligne le décalage entre les progrès enregistrés dans la féminisation de certaines administrations et les difficultés plus larges rencontrées par les femmes pour accéder à l’emploi au Maroc. La fonction publique apparaît ainsi comme un espace où leur présence s’est renforcée, sans pour autant traduire une amélioration générale de leur insertion professionnelle. The post Fonction publique : les femmes dominent dans la santé et la justice, mais restent minoritaires dans l’emploi appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Ogun to convert 6,000 Amotekun, So-Safe personnel to state police — Abiodun
items.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun, has said the state is ready for the establishment of its own police force, disclosing that more than 6,000 personnel of the Ogun State Security Network, known as Amotekun, and the So-Safe Corps are available to provide the manpower for the proposed outfit. Abiodun said his administration had laid a solid foundation for state policing through the establishment of community-based security structures, noting that the existing personnel and operational experience of the two outfits would facilitate the transition. The governor spoke at the 50th anniversary celebration of Ereke Day in Ikenne, Ikenne Local Government Area of the state, where he described the Ogun State House of Assembly’s approval of the establishment of state police as a significant step towards strengthening security and protecting lives and property. Abiodun, who chairs the Nigeria Governors’ Forum Committee on State Police Creation and represents President Bola Tinubu on the committee, expressed confidence in the state’s readiness to implement the initiative. He said: “I am the Chairman of the Governors’ Forum on State Police Creation and the representative of the President in the Governors’ Forum on State Police Creation. I am proud to announce that the Ogun State House of Assembly has approved the creation of state police. “Between Amotekun and So-Safe Corps, we have over 6,000 personnel. We are ready for the Ogun State Police Command, and that will make the difference in protecting the lives and property of our people.” The governor stressed that security was essential to economic prosperity, investment and sustainable development, adding that meaningful progress could only be achieved in an atmosphere of peace and stability. He called for sustained collaboration between communities and security agencies to ensure the safety of residents, businesses and investors across the state. In a related development, Abiodun directed the immediate reconstruction of the Delabo-Ikenne Road, assuring residents that the project would improve accessibility, enhance connectivity and stimulate economic activities in the community. Speaking on the golden jubilee of Ereke Day, the governor described the 50-year celebration as a significant milestone reflecting the unity, common heritage and shared aspirations of the people of Ikenne. “Fifty years is very remarkable in the tradition and history of any people. It speaks to a united and common heritage, shared values and a collective determination to build a better future,” he said. He commended traditional rulers and the Ikenne Traditional Council of Chiefs for their leadership and commitment to preserving the community’s cultural identity while promoting development. Abiodun also congratulated the people for sustaining the annual celebration over five decades, describing the achievement as a testament to the foresight of their forebears, the sacrifices of successive generations and the strength of their communal spirit. He noted that Ereke Day had evolved beyond a cultural celebration into a platform for intellectual engagement, institutional development, infrastructural advancement and the preservation of the community’s heritage. The governor particularly praised the Ikenne Community Development Association for mobilising the human, intellectual and financial resources of indigenes to address the community’s developmental needs. According to him, while government has a responsibility to provide leadership and create an enabling environment, sustainable development also requires active participation and ownership by the people. Describing Ikenne as a community of historical importance to Ogun State and Nigeria, Abiodun recalled its association with prominent national figures, including the late nationalist and statesman, Chief Obafemi Awolowo, and renowned educationist, Dr Tai Solarin. He said their contributions to education, democratic governance and national development remained enduring legacies for younger generations to emulate. Providing an update on his administration’s infrastructural interventions, Abiodun disclosed that more than 1,700 kilometres of roads had been constructed and rehabilitated across the state, including over 40 roads in Remoland. He said the projects were aimed at improving transportation networks, opening up rural communities, enhancing connectivity and stimulating economic activities. The governor, however, maintained that infrastructural development must go hand in hand with peace and security, stressing that no society could make meaningful progress without a stable environment. He also urged youths in Ikenne to shun political violence and resist attempts by politicians to use them as instruments of violence ahead of the 2027 general elections. “No political ambition is worth the peace of our community, and no temporary inducement is worth sacrificing your future,” he cautioned. Abiodun urged the youths to demonstrate political maturity, patriotism and responsible civic engagement, insisting that electoral contests should be based on ideas, credible leadership, performance and issue-based campaigns rather than intimidation and violence. He also appealed to traditional rulers, community leaders, professionals and Ikenne indigenes in the diaspora to sustain their contributions to the development of their ancestral community. Earlier, the Chairman of the occasion, Mr Kunle Soname, described Abiodun as a worthy son of Remoland and commended his administration’s contributions to Ikenne’s development. Soname specifically acknowledged the governor’s donation of a 500KVA transformer and the reconstruction of Awolowo Road, alongside other developmental interventions. He assured Abiodun of the continued support and cooperation of the people of Ikenne and Remoland, expressing confidence in the administration’s commitment to the area’s development. items.title: Judicial Service staff extend indefinite strike as gov’t fails to respond to final demands
items.description: The Judicial Service Staff Association of Ghana (JUSAG) and the Judicial Service Staff Association of Ghana’s Union (SSAJUG) have announced that their indefinite strike will continue on Monday, November 9, following the failure of the government and the Judicial Service management to respond to their revised demands. The two unions said they had engaged the government and the management of the Judicial Service over the past few days in an attempt to resolve the dispute and reach an agreement that would address workers’ concerns while taking into account the government’s financial constraints. However, as of 4:00 p.m. on Sunday, November 8, the unions said they had not received any official response from either the government or the management of the Judicial Service. In a statement issued on Sunday, November 8 and signed by JUSAG General Secretary Abdulai Yakubu and SSAJUG General Secretary George Taylor, the unions said they submitted their final demands to government on Thursday, November 5, describing the revised proposal as the best position they could offer to improve workers’ living conditions and restore effective justice delivery. “The unions communicated their final demand to the government on Thursday, 5th November, 2026, stating that the revised position is the best the unions can come through to improve the living conditions of staff and restore justice delivery,” the statement said. The unions consequently maintained that their members would remain on strike until their demands were met. “As at 4:00 pm on Sunday, November 8, 2026, no official feedback was received from either the government or management of the Judicial Service,” they stated. The unions have also directed all Judicial Service staff, including those working at the Supreme Court, to stay away from work throughout the strike. They said that the industrial action would remain in force until an agreement was reached and workers were satisfied with the outcome. “Notice is further served that all staff, including members serving at the Supreme Court, shall stay away from work during the pendency of the strike,” the statement said. The unions acknowledged the inconvenience the continued industrial action would cause members of the public and institutions that depend on Judicial Service operations. However, they said the working conditions of their members had made it difficult for them to continue providing services. “While we empathise with the people of Ghana and the institutions who require our services, our present conditions make it impossible for us to render our services,” they stated. They added that their members would only return to work when their demands had been met, and staff were adequately satisfied and motivated. “We shall return when our demands are met, and staff are highly satisfied and motivated,” the statement added. items.title: Agriculture algérienne : Tebboune ordonne une vaste réforme en 10 mesures radicales
items.description: Le président de la République Abdelmadjid Tebboune a pris 10 mesures radicales pour une réforme profonde de l’agriculture algérienne. Présidant ce dimanche 8 novembre une réunion du conseil des ministres, le chef de l’Etat a donné au gouvernement des instructions et des orientations qui s'apparentent à une refonte du fonctionnement du secteur agricole. La réunion du conseil des ministres est consacrée à l’examen d’un exposé sur la situation actuelle et les perspectives du secteur, comme cela avait été prévu lors de la réunion du conseil le 4 octobre dernier. Le président a donné ses instructions détaillées après avoir entendu et “salué” un exposé “approfondi” présenté par le ministre de l’Agriculture, Sid Ali Khaldi, en pleine crise de la pomme de la terre qui a montré les failles de l’agriculture algérienne. Un plan d’organisation de l’agriculture et un service dédié aux statistiques La première instruction de Abdelmadjid Tebboune concerne l’élaboration d’un “nouveau plan d’organisation locale de l’agriculture, afin d’assurer une plus grande transparence et des statistiques plus précises et plus modernes”, lit-on dans un communiqué de la présidence de la République. Toujours en ce qui concerne les chiffres, il a ordonné la création “immédiate” d’un service dédié aux statistiques, “couvrant l’ensemble des activités et des métiers liés au secteur agricole”, dans le but de mettre fin à toutes les formes de “retard dans l’approvisionnement du marché national en produits de consommation, en particulier les produits de grande consommation”. L’autre décision du président concerne la création d’un office dédié aux légumineuses sèches et au stockage des céréales, relevant de la compétence de l’Office algérien professionnel des céréales (OAIC). Une réorganisation du ministère est aussi à prévoir. Le ministre de l’Agriculture est chargé d’élaborer un plan de répartition des missions du secteur de la pêche et celles du secteur des forêts entre un ministre délégué chargé de la Pêche et un secrétaire d’État chargé des Forêts. Interdiction de la mise en jachère des terres et de l’utilisation du maïs comme fourrage La prochaine récolte doit être préparée dès maintenant. Le président de la République a ordonné de commencer, dès le mois de novembre en cours, la mise à disposition du matériel agricole nécessaire, “tant en quantité qu’en qualité, pour toutes les zones de production”, et cela après la mise en œuvre de la décision du conseil des ministres relative à la création de coopératives de mécanisation. La mise en jachère des terres sera désormais interdite en Algérie, sur décision du président Tebboune, qui a estimé qu’il s'agit de “pratiques fondées sur des arguments erronés qui n’ont aucun rapport avec l’agriculture moderne et contemporaine”. L’autre interdiction “totale” prononcée concerne l’utilisation du maïs comme fourrage vert pour l'alimentation du bétail. La pratique “n’a en aucun cas eu d’effet positif sur la production de viande ni sur la satisfaction des besoins du marché national”. Elle a, “au contraire, entraîné une grave pénurie du maïs en grain”. Lutte contre les fraudes et la rétention de la production Dans un contexte de spéculation sur certains produits comme la pomme de terre, le chef de l’Etat a insisté sur la nécessité de lutter contre “toutes les formes de rétention de la production agricole par les agriculteurs”, d’autant plus que, a-t-il souligné, l’État a “largement ouvert la voie à l’achat des récoltes agricoles stratégiques aux meilleurs prix”. Tout comme il a ordonné de lutter contre toutes les formes de fraude dans le secteur agricole, “de la production à la distribution et à l’approvisionnement.” Tout en instruisant de réexaminer le fonctionnement et l’organisation des entreprises relevant du secteur agricole, ainsi que la pertinence de leurs rôles, le président de la République a chargé le ministre de l’Agriculture de préparer un exposé spécifique, qu’il présentera à nouveau devant le conseil des ministres, sur l’état d’avancement de la mise en œuvre de ces recommandations et sur les effets de l’entrée en vigueur de la loi-cadre agricole. items.title: Enugu pensioners recount past ordeals as Mbah pays 26-year gratuity arrears
items.description: …Pensioners hail governor as promise keeper . ..Mbah: No retiree should go to bed hungry Enugu State pensioners under the auspices of the Nigeria Union of Pensioners (NUP) have hailed Governor Peter Mbah for keeping his campaign promise to clear legacy arrears, describing their decades of disappointment after serving their fatherland as a harrowing experience. The pensioners spoke as retirees started receiving their gratuities dating back to the year 2000, with some also extending to the military era, saying the development had restored life to their bodies. The Chairman, Enugu State chapter of NUP, Ikechukwu Ekere, confirmed the development at the weekend, describing it as “an emotional moment for pensioners, many of whom had long given up hope of receiving their gratuities in their lifetime.” “Yes, I can confirm to you that our members have started receiving the alerts. Governor Mbah is a promise keeper; he has done it again and we can’t thank him enough,” he said. In the same vein, the Caretaker Chairman of the Nigeria Union of Pensioners, Local Government Staff Pensions Board Branch, Kenneth Ugwueze, told journalists that the development had restored hope and joy in many homes, saying that Mbah had, once again, proven himself as a leader who could be trusted. “You know what it means for a governor to pay debts incurred by many governors before him? It takes a large quantity of milk of human kindness. We are happy to see a day like this in our lifetime. We will continue to pray for him. “We are also grateful and happy with the new dimensions brought in by our governor in pension administration, especially in the local government system. “Before now, local government workers and primary school teachers who retired had to wait for two years before receiving their pensions. But since the conclusion of the verification exercise in July 2024, no pensioner in the local government system has been denied pension. We have been receiving our pensions as and when due. “Now that our people have started receiving alerts for their gratuity, it is a thing of joy,” he said. Some beneficiaries of the ongoing payments also expressed gratitude to the governor, describing the development as a rekindling of hope after years and devades of waiting. They said previous governments had not paid them even in the days of excess crude revenues. Mr. Luke Obi Ezea, who retired in 2014, said he had since resigned himself to fate and put everything in the hands of God. “I put in 35 years in service. Already, I had put everything in the hands of God because previous governors had made promises, but to no avail. They were just empty promises at the end of their eight years. But Peter Mbah is an action governor and keeps his word,” he stated. Mr. Sunday Nwadi, a 2015 retiree, described Mbah as a godly and listening governor who does not play politics with the welfare of his people. “I am enjoying today because, apart from this gratuity, he is not owing monthly pensions. He is up to date. He is not like the others, who would owe us pensions for many months. Nothing will happen to Mbah. He is returning for a second term.” Susanna Emehelu, whose husband retired in 2013, said the man had been sick for a long time, and they had been hoping against hope that the gratuity would come to help ameliorate their challenges. “When I broke the good news to him, he was so happy and asked me to rush to the office to confirm. Now, he is so happy that he would eat the fruits of his labour in his lifetime. May God bless our governor,” she stated. Mr. Paul Ozoeze, a 2010 retiree, said the gratuity payment had restored life to his body, noting that it had been nearly 20 years of suffering for him. Meanwhile, the Accountant-General of Enugu State, Mr. Tony Okenwa, recalled that Mbah had always insisted during discussions leading up to the verification and payment of backlogs that no senior citizen should go to bed hungry. “These are old debts. Some of them date back even to the military era. But the governor has said that no retiree will stay without receiving his or her pension and gratuity, and he is very passionate about it. “Whenever I went to him, he would ask: ‘Do you mean that people retire and then don’t go home with their gratuity?’ “He could not understand how somebody would work for many years, retire and still not receive what he had earned,” Okenwa said. He said the State Executive Council, after several layers of verification, approved N32bn, with the governor releasing an initial N10bn, assuring that the releases would continue until the entire liabilities were cleared. The post Enugu pensioners recount past ordeals as Mbah pays 26-year gratuity arrears appeared first on Vanguard News .

Minority alleges 300 Ghanaians travelled abroad on passports obtained through an illegal scheme
items.description: The Minority in Parliament has alleged that approximately 300 Ghanaians have travelled to Europe and other destinations using diplomatic and service passports purportedly obtained through an arrangement involving officials of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Passport Office. According to the Minority, the alleged arrangement involved a travel and tour business through which customers paid money to obtain the special passports, despite not qualifying under the law to hold them. Addressing a press conference in Parliament on Sunday, November 8, the Ranking Member on Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee, Samuel Abu Jinapor, identified one Ibrahim Wallee as the person managing the travel and tour business in Ghana, with Bright Yeboah Owusu serving as his agent in Europe. Mr Jinapor alleged that applicants were assigned official positions and designations they did not occupy, or which did not exist, to facilitate their passport applications. He further claimed that some officials assisted beneficiaries at the airport to avoid or minimise scrutiny by immigration officers. “As at now, our sources indicate that some 300 Ghanaians have travelled to Europe and other destinations using diplomatic and service passports allegedly issued through this arrangement,” he said. The Minority is calling for a parliamentary investigation to establish the number of people involved, how the alleged operation was facilitated and whether public officials benefited financially. The Minority’s press conference, which was advertised earlier, came a few hours after the Foreign Affairs Ministry issued a statement to clarify the allegations. In that statement, the Ministry said it had revoked 10 Service Passports allegedly obtained through an illegal arrangement involving a syndicate operating within the passport administration system. The affected documents were issued between January 2023 and August 2026 to individuals who, according to preliminary investigations, did not meet the requirements for obtaining Service Passports. It added that the beneficiaries were being pursued, including two individuals who allegedly travelled abroad using the illegally acquired documents in 2023. Read Also: 10 illegally issued Service Passports cancelled as Foreign Affairs Ministry pursues beneficiaries The Ministry’s investigations followed two petitions received on October 8, 2026, prompting the establishment of an investigative committee on October 13, on the instructions of Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa. The Ministry’s statement also announced that the Acting Director of Passports, Mahama Yahaya Amantana, and a junior Foreign Service Officer, Alhassan Sumani, have been interdicted and referred to the Ghana Police Service for further investigations and possible prosecution.

The persons who provided them say these were payments made for the diplomatic and service passports and the promised travel arrangements,” Mr Jinapor stated. The Minority alleged that the payments were made through an arrangement managed in Ghana by Ibrahim Wallee, with Owusu serving as an agent in Europe. It said the records would be submitted to Parliament as part of its evidence for the proposed investigation. The Minority’s press conference, which was advertised earlier, came a few hours after the Foreign Affairs Ministry issued a statement to clarify the allegations. items.title: Minority to file motion for parliamentary probe into alleged sale of diplomatic, service passports
items.description: The Minority in Parliament will, on Monday, November 9, file a motion seeking the establishment of an Ad Hoc Committee to investigate allegations of irregular issuance and sale of Ghanaian diplomatic and service passports. The Minority says it has uncovered documents suggesting that some individuals who did not qualify for the special travel documents were allegedly presented as public officials of various state institutions to facilitate their acquisition. Addressing a press conference in Parliament on Sunday, November 8, the Ranking Member on Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee, Samuel Abu Jinapor, said the allegations raised serious concerns about the integrity of Ghana’s official travel documents and required an independent investigation. “Our purpose is to secure an independent parliamentary inquiry in which the available material can be examined, witnesses heard, and all persons concerned afforded a fair opportunity to respond,” he stated. The proposed committee is expected to examine passport approvals and issuances from January 7, 2025, to the date the motion is adopted, establish the extent of the alleged irregularities and identify persons responsible. The Minority is also seeking access to passport applications, approval letters, payment records and relevant communications. The Minority’s press conference, which was advertised earlier, came a few hours after the Foreign Affairs Ministry issued a statement to clarify the allegations. In that statement, the Ministry said it had revoked 10 Service Passports allegedly obtained through an illegal arrangement involving a syndicate operating within the passport administration system. The affected documents were issued between January 2023 and August 2026 to individuals who, according to preliminary investigations, did not meet the requirements for obtaining Service Passports. It added that the beneficiaries were being pursued, including two individuals who allegedly travelled abroad using the illegally acquired documents in 2023. items.title: Sudan fuel shortages damage crops in El Gezira as food prices soar, bakeries strike in North Kordofan
items.description: Fuel shortages and soaring production costs are damaging agricultural crops in Sudan’s El Gezira state, while rising food and transport prices are placing further pressure on household budgets. Reports of a general strike by bakeries in El Obeid, the capital of North Kordofan, has disrupted bread supplies amid a dispute over production costs and bread prices. A farmer in the El Gezira agricultural scheme, identified as Mohammed, told Radio Dabanga that large areas of the maize crop had been damaged because of a shortage of petrol needed to operate irrigation pumps. He said the price of a four-gallon container of petrol had reached SDG600,000, forcing him to search for fuel outside the state to save the remainder of his crop. He warned that declining agricultural production could further deepen food insecurity and hunger. ‘Food and transport costs soar’ Food prices have also risen sharply across markets in El Gezira, including those in El Maseed, El Ma’aliq and El Kamlin. Ahmed Mohammed El Khair, a resident of the state, told Radio Dabanga that the prices of essential commodities , particularly maize, lentils, sesame and wheat, had witnessed sharp increases. He said a sack of maize now costs between SDG800,000 and SDG820,000, while a sack of wheat has reached around SDG780,000. Lentils sell for SDG850,000 per sack, while Kabkabiya (type of legume) costs between SDG300,000 and SDG450,000. A sack of sesame has reached SDG860,000, while Egyptian beans cost between SDG1.1 million and SDG1.2 million, depending on the size and quality of the beans. El Khair said the price increases had severely affected residents’ purchasing power and reduced market activity, as most people had low or no incomes. He described the situation as a serious concern for residents and called on government authorities to intervene. Transport costs have also surged, with the cost of transporting goods in Omdurman exceeding SDG2 million. In Kassala, taxi fares have reached SDG20,000 per passenger, adding to the growing cost of living. ‘Bakeries strike in El Obeid’ All bakeries in El Obeid have closed in a general strike over a dispute with local authorities concerning bread prices and rising production costs . Journalist Omar Mohammed Omar told Radio Dabanga that the complete shutdown had disrupted bread supplies across the city, leaving residents struggling to access a basic food staple. He criticised the size and quality of the bread being sold, saying the loaves did not meet the expected standards. He said bread prices had previously reached SDG2,000 and, in some cases, SDG3,000, amid demands for prices to reflect the actual weight, size and nutritional value of each loaf. The strike has disrupted daily life in El Obeid, particularly for families and schoolchildren who depend on bread for breakfast. items.title: Gaz : l’AIE pointe l’exposition du Maroc aux chocs de prix
items.description: L’Agence internationale de l’énergie range le Royaume parmi les économies africaines qui recourent le plus au gaz importé, alors que le marché mondial est secoué par les perturbations du GNL au détroit d’Ormuz. Dans le Global Gas Security Review 2026, l’Agence internationale de l’énergie (AIE) classe le Maroc parmi les pays du continent qui recourent le plus aux importations de gaz naturel. Ce positionnement rend le Royaume plus sensible aux mouvements des cours mondiaux comme aux limites de ses infrastructures, dans un marché en pleine agitation. L’origine de ces turbulences tient aux perturbations des flux de gaz naturel liquéfié (GNL) passant par le détroit d’Ormuz. Entre mars et octobre, les chargements en provenance du Qatar et des Émirats arabes unis ont reculé de plus de 60 milliards de mètres cubes par rapport à la même période de 2025. L’augmentation de la production en Amérique du Nord et en Afrique n’a compensé cette contraction que partiellement. Pour l’ensemble de l’année, l’AIE anticipe une baisse d’environ 3% de l’offre mondiale de GNL, soit près de 20 milliards de mètres cubes, ce qui constituerait le plus fort repli jamais enregistré sur douze mois. Les prix ont suivi. Sur le marché européen TTF, ils ont progressé de près de 70% sur un an entre mars et octobre, pour s’établir en moyenne autour de 20 dollars par million d’unités thermiques britanniques (MBtu). En Asie, les prix spot du GNL ont bondi de près de 80%, à 21,5 dollars par MBtu en moyenne. Cette flambée pèse sur la consommation mondiale de gaz, attendue en recul de 1,5% en 2026, soit environ 65 milliards de mètres cubes, l’électricité et l’industrie étant parmi les principaux secteurs concernés. Sur le continent, les producteurs adossés à leurs propres ressources ont mieux amorti le choc que les acheteurs extérieurs, confrontés à des factures alourdies et à des cargaisons plus difficiles à obtenir. L’AIE inclut le Royaume dans ce second groupe. L’Afrique évolue d’ailleurs à contre-courant de la tendance mondiale. Là où la consommation planétaire de gaz doit reculer cette année, celle du continent devrait grimper d’environ 5%, tirée surtout par la production d’électricité et les activités du secteur énergétique. Entre 2020 et 2025, elle avait déjà progressé de 1,7% par an en moyenne, portée par la croissance démographique, l’essor des besoins en électricité et le développement industriel. L’Afrique ne pèse cependant que 4% de la consommation mondiale, et cette demande reste très concentrée : trois pays, dont l’Égypte et le Nigeria, totalisent à eux seuls plus des trois quarts des volumes consommés. Une bonne partie du gaz africain est pensée pour l’export : les installations tournées vers les marchés internationaux sont plus abouties que les réseaux domestiques. Sur le littoral, des terminaux de regazéification encore peu étendus et des réseaux morcelés freinent la diffusion du GNL ou du gaz de gazoduc importé. L’AIE conditionne l’essor de ces marchés à des investissements, du traitement du gaz à la distribution en passant par les gazoducs et les centrales, et à la présence de clients capables de payer. Pour le Royaume, l’enjeu ne se réduit donc pas aux quantités : encore faut-il que les routes d’approvisionnement et de transport correspondent aux usages. L’étude ne chiffre ni la consommation ni les importations du Royaume pour 2026. Elle offre plutôt une grille de lecture d’un continent où l’accès au gaz varie fortement d’un pays à l’autre, et met deux chantiers sur la table : élargir les sources d’approvisionnement et étoffer les infrastructures. Pour l’AIE, la répétition des crises plaide pour une coopération internationale plus étroite et des investissements sur l’ensemble de la filière, l’objectif étant que les importateurs absorbent les secousses de prix et d’approvisionnement sans que leurs marchés de l’énergie n’en sortent durablement affaiblis. The post Gaz : l’AIE pointe l’exposition du Maroc aux chocs de prix appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Un pharmacien assassiné à Constantine, le Snapo réclame des mesures
items.description: Drame à Constantine. Un pharmacien a été assassiné, a dénoncé, ce dimanche dans un communiqué, le bureau national du Syndicat national des pharmaciens d'officine (Snapo). Le syndicat a exprimé sa « profonde tristesse », son « immense affliction » et sa « vive indignation » à la suite du « crime » ayant coûté la vie à leur confrère, le pharmacien Mounir Nasri. Le drame a eu lieu dans le quartier de Daksi, dans le centre-ville de Constantine, selon la même source. Les circonstances de cet assassinat n’ont pas été évoquées, mais le Snapo laisse entendre que ce crime est lié au trafic de psychotropes . « Il s'agit d'un événement tragique qui a bouleversé la famille pharmaceutique et suscité une grande tristesse ainsi qu'une vive inquiétude parmi les professionnels du secteur », a indiqué le Snapo. Ce dernier a exprimé sa « ferme condamnation de cette agression criminelle, ainsi que de toutes les formes de violence et d'attaques pouvant viser les pharmaciens dans l'exercice de leurs fonctions ». Le Snapo réclame des « mesures supplémentaires urgentes » Son bureau national a estimé que la protection du pharmacien et la sécurisation des officines sont devenues une « nécessité impérieuse ». « Cela exige la mise en œuvre de mesures supplémentaires et urgentes, compte tenu du rôle vital que jouent les officines au service de la santé publique et de la continuité de la prise en charge des citoyens », a réclamé le Snapo. Le syndicat national des pharmaciens d’officine a lancé un appel aux pouvoirs publics et aux autorités compétentes pour « renforcer les dispositifs de sécurité visant à protéger les officines et leur personnel, et à garantir les conditions nécessaires permettant au pharmacien d'exercer ses missions dans un environnement sûr, préservant sa dignité et son intégrité physique ». Il a également réitéré sa demande « d'accélérer la mise en place et l'activation de la plateforme numérique dédiée à la gestion et au suivi des ordonnances médicales pour les médicaments ayant des propriétés psychotropes, conformément aux dispositions de l'article 5 bis 8 de la loi n° 23-05 ». Cela implique, a-t-il ajouté, de « finaliser les textes ainsi que les procédures réglementaires et techniques nécessaires à sa mise en service dans les plus brefs délais ». Le Snapo pointe le danger des psychotropes sur les pharmaciens Pour le Snapo, l'adoption de cette plateforme numérique permettrait de « renforcer les mécanismes de contrôle et de traçabilité, de limiter la falsification des ordonnances et la mauvaise utilisation de ces médicaments, tout en assurant aux pharmaciens la protection nécessaire contre les pressions, les pratiques illégales et les risques auxquels ils pourraient être exposés dans l'accomplissement de leur devoir professionnel ». Le Bureau national du Snapo a exprimé, en outre, sa « pleine confiance » en la justice algérienne ainsi qu’en les institutions de l’État. Il dit attendre que les enquêtes « suivent leur cours afin de faire toute la lumière sur les circonstances de ce crime, d’établir les responsabilités et d’infliger à l’auteur les sanctions prévues par la loi ». La sécurité et l’intégrité physique du pharmacien « ne constituent pas une simple revendication professionnelle ou syndicale ; elles sont une condition indispensable pour garantir la continuité d’un service de santé essentiel et pour protéger le droit des citoyens à accéder aux soins pharmaceutiques dans des conditions sûres », a conclu le Snapo. items.title: On SNL , the Struggle (For Power) Was Real
items.description: This season of Saturday Night Live has gotten a lot of mileage from inaction. Week after week, sketch after sketch—as James Austin Johnson’s version of Donald Trump interrupts whatever comedy might be at play—the show’s performers have done more than merely step aside as the president storms the stage. Instead, his presence leaves them comically petrified: frozen, at pretty much the moment of his entrance, unable to do anything else. Like much of what plays out on live TV, the gag works because, so often, it doesn’t quite; half the fun is watching stars such as Kenan Thompson, temporarily transformed into audience members, trying to stifle their laughter while Johnson Trumps it up. The freeze-frame device also works, though, because of its upstager in chief. Few jokes capture the president’s scene-stealing capabilities better than ones that find Trump like a modern-day Medusa, turning everyone in his path to stone. There’s a fine line, however, between running joke and crutch—and it’s one that SNL has frequently crossed. Only five episodes into the current season, the freeze-frame bits have become notably tepid. But on last night’s episode, the freeze frames were not just the point; they made a point. The cold open was an inevitable recap of the midterm elections: the blue wave that, on Tuesday, swept the country. The sketch’s action began in expected fashion, with the Senate Democrats Hakeem Jeffries (played by Thompson) and Chuck Schumer (Sarah Sherman) celebrating, and analyzing, their party’s landslide victory. How did they do it? What was the source of their historic rebuke to Trump, the MAGA coalition, and the political status quo? “ Me !” said Trump, storming the stage. Johnson’s version of the president blathered (about Millennial cringe, about the long-gone sitcom New Girl , about men’s backsides); Colin Jost, as Pete Hegseth, at one point smarmed onto the scene. All along, Jeffries and Schumer were relegated to the background, present but vacant: two power players rendered awkwardly inert. The staging made sense—because the up staging made sense. The sketch, dominated by Trump even in his moment of loss, hinted at Democrats’ famed ability to snatch defeat from the jaws of victory. It also visualized the fickle workings of American party politics. Power, particularly in this moment, is largely a function of attention: a matter of which politician can occupy the forefront of voters’ screens and minds. The sketch, as each character jockeyed for eyeballs, managed to turn that reality into comedy. American politics is a battle of attrition; last night, on SNL , the (power) struggle was real. The episode’s host made that opening salvo especially apt. The comedian Druski has made a specialty out of skewering the politics of race (which he brought with him to the show, including to a sketch co-starring Andrew Dismukes as a fictional Atlantic reporter) and rose to fame posting comedy videos to Instagram. He is the first digital creator to host SNL . His episode’s cold open fittingly, and elegantly, mimicked the workings of the phone screen and the brute dynamics of the digital economy. Images, vying for primacy: That’s how information works now. It’s how culture works now. It’s how politics work now. Candidates battle not just to convince voters that their way is the right way but also to simply be there, crowding out the other contenders—undeniable, unavoidable, and ever in the foreground. The sketch, in recognition of that, anointed a new scene stealer: Senator-Elect James Talarico, whose victory this week helped turn Texas blue. Operating in another long-standing SNL tradition, Talarico made a surprise cameo, closing out the sketch by upstaging everyone else, literally and symbolically. The lame-duck executive, the leaders of the legislative establishment—for the first time in a long time, they were relegated to the background as the young politician talked about a new day in American politics. “It’s clear people want something new,” Talarico announced, grinning, as SNL ’s live audience whooped in approval. But true change—real transformation—is more easily scripted than done. And before Talarico shouted the customary “Live from New York” tagline, he ended his appearance with a joke that, ironically but perhaps appropriately, upstaged his own message. Americans want something different, he said, before getting to the punch line: “I’m talking, of course, about SNL ’s cold opens.”

items.title: Élim CAN 2027 : Nabil Neghiz vise "au moins un point" face à "la meilleure équipe d’Afrique"
items.description: En l'absence de stade homologué à Niamey, le Niger s’apprête à disputer ses deux prochains matches des éliminatoires de la Coupe d’Afrique des Nations (CAN) 2027 directement au Maroc, à Casablanca et Rabat. Face aux Lions de l'Atlas, le sélectionneur algérien du Mena, Nabil Neghiz, aborde cette double confrontation avec réalisme mais sans complexe, fixant un objectif comptable clair à ses hommes. Privée de rencontres à domicile depuis novembre 2021 en raison des travaux de réhabilitation du stade Général Seyni-Kountché, la sélection nigérienne s'est habituée à évoluer sur terrain neutre. Toutefois, la proximité géographique entre Casablanca et Rabat constitue un soulagement logistique pour le staff technique : « en septembre, nous avions rencontré et battu le Lesotho (2-1, le 25 septembre) à Accra, au Ghana, avant d’aller affronter le Gabon à Franceville (défaite 2-0, le 29 septembre), ce qui sous-entend des voyages longs, un temps de récupération limité et peu d’entraînements. C’est l’avantage de jouer ces deux rencontres au Maroc, même si nous aurions préféré évoluer devant notre public », a indiqué le technicien algérien. Conscient de l'écart qui sépare les deux formations, le Niger s'étant incliné face aux Lions de l'Atlas en 2025 à Oujda (1-2) et Rabat (0-5) lors des éliminatoires du Mondial 2026, Nabil Neghiz ne tarit pas d'éloges sur son adversaire : « affronter chez elle la meilleure sélection d’Afrique, quart de finaliste de la Coupe du monde, cela s’annonce compliqué. C’est une équipe très forte, certains de ses joueurs, tels Brahim Diaz, Achraf Hakimi, Ismael Saibari entre autres, évoluent dans les meilleurs clubs du monde, au Real Madrid, au PSG, au Bayern. A domicile, le Maroc est redoutable. Il l’est aussi à l’extérieur. On sait ce qui nous attend ». Malgré ce déséquilibre sur le papier, le patron du Mena, qui espère ramener le Niger en phase finale continentale pour la première fois depuis 2013, refuse de se présenter en victime expiatoire. « Le Maroc et le Gabon sont les favoris, mais on se doit d’avoir des objectifs. Avant les deux dernières journées en mars, il faudrait arriver à prendre au moins un point contre les Lions de l’Atlas. Nous savons que ce sera compliqué, que nous n’aurons pas souvent le ballon, mais il faudra savoir gérer les temps forts des Marocains, comme les nôtres », dit-il. Face à l'armada marocaine, Neghiz mise sur la force collective et la résilience de son groupe pour déjouer les pronostics : « nous savons que les Marocains sont supérieurs, mais nous avons nos qualités techniques, physiques et mentales. Mes joueurs sont fiers de porter le maillot de leur pays et ils donnent tout, à chaque match ». The post Élim CAN 2027 : Nabil Neghiz vise "au moins un point" face à "la meilleure équipe d’Afrique" appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Train collision in Egypt kills at least 7, injures dozens, health ministry says
items.description: CAIRO, Nov 8 (Reuters) - Two passenger trains collided some 76 km (47 miles) south of Cairo on Sunday, killing at least seven people and injuring 112, Egypt’s health ministry said. The state railway authority said a train travelling from Giza to Fayoum hit the back of another heading from Cairo to Aswan, derailing several carriages. Emergency crews were clearing the wreckage to restore services on the Cairo-Upper Egypt line, the railway authority said, without giving any indication of how long this would take.

items.title: Netanyahu rival Eisenkot seeks 'wide' government but path to power uncertain
items.description: By Steven Scheer JERUSALEM, Nov 8 (Reuters) - Former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot said on Sunday he will work to form a wide government as quickly as possible, but his path to power was uncertain following a deadlocked election that failed to dislodge Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Israeli President Isaac Herzog on Saturday gave Eisenkot the first opportunity to try to form a new government after the October 27 election left both Eisenkot and Netanyahu short of the majority needed to govern.

items.title: Taekwondo : 80 pratiquants réussissent les épreuves de passage de grade
items.description: Lomé, 8 nov. (ATOP) – La Fédération togolaise de taekwondo (FTTKD) a organisé un examen de passage de grade, du Dan (ceinture) 1 au Dan 4, le dimanche 8 novembre à Lomé. Au total, 80 candidats ont réussi les différentes épreuves, en attendant la proclamation officielle des résultats prévue dans deux semaines. Une trentaine de clubs ont pris part à cette évaluation qui a enregistré une centaine de candidats, dont une vingtaine de filles et de femmes. Parmi eux, 54 aspirent au Dan 1, 16 au Dan 2, 16 au Dan 3 et 14 au Dan 4. L’examen vise à améliorer les mouvements et le niveau technique des pratiquants. Les candidats ont compéti dans plusieurs disciplines, notamment le Kibon (mouvements de base), le Poumsea (formes de défense et d’attaque), le Hoshinsul (défense contre les saisies), les techniques d’attaque et de défense, le Kyukpa (casse), les coups de pied, le Kyurigi (combats) et la théorie portant sur les noms des mouvements. Les postulants au Dan 4 ont également présenté, la veille, une soutenance de dix minutes sur un thème de leur choix. Les candidats de moins de 16 ans ont été soumis aux épreuves du Poom, tandis que ceux âgés de 17 ans et plus ont concouru pour les grades supérieurs. Au Kyurigi, les postulants au Dan 1 se sont affrontés entre eux et avec un candidat. Ceux du Dan 2 ont combattu entre eux et contre deux athlètes de ceinture rouge. Pour les Dan 3 et 4, les combats ont également opposé les candidats à trois ceintures noires. A l’épreuve de casse, les moins de 16 ans ont brisé une planche en bois, contre deux planches pour les candidats aux Dan 2, 3 et 4. Le président de la FTTKD, Boyodi Hénoc, s’est réjoui de la tenue de cet examen, après deux années sans organisation de passage de grade. Il a expliqué que cette initiative vise à relever le niveau des athlètes qui s’entraînent régulièrement. En prélude à cette session, les candidats ont suivi un stage de deux semaines pour mieux se préparer aux différentes épreuves. « Après l’étape de Lomé, ce sera l’étape du nord le 15 novembre prochain, suivie d’une compétition de fin d’année, dont la date sera communiquée ultérieurement. Je voudrais encourager les pratiquants à ne pas lâcher, à continuer les entraînements. Quand on lance des stages, qu’ils viennent pour parfaire leurs mouvements. Sinon, ils risquent de ne pas évoluer », a déclaré le président. Pour l’instructeur et coach international, Dégboé Josélito Léonidase, le niveau des candidats est acceptable, malgré l’interruption des activités depuis plus de deux ans, qui a entraîné un relâchement chez certains athlètes. Il a invité les bonnes volontés à soutenir les clubs en organisant des compétitions interclubs ou des tournois à quatre ou huit participants. Selon lui, ces rencontres offrent aux jeunes pratiquants des occasions de se mesurer et de maintenir leur condition physique. Il a toutefois souligné la nécessité d’informer la fédération du bien-fondé de toute compétition avant son organisation. ATOP/AR/AO

items.title: Mahama congratulates Rev. Stephen Wengam on second term as Assemblies of God, Ghana leader
items.description: President John Mahama has congratulated Reverend Dr Stephen Yenusom Wengam on his inauguration for a second four-year term as General Superintendent of the Assemblies of God, Ghana. He commended Rev. Dr Wengam for his transformational leadership during his first term, particularly the implementation of the Church’s Transformation Agenda, which has resulted in the planting of more than 2,000 churches and the training of over 440 pastors. President Mahama, who is a member of the Assemblies of God, Ghana, together with First Lady Lordina Mahama, gave the commendation at the inauguration of Rev. Dr Wengam and members of the Church’s Executive Presbytery in Accra. He said Rev. Dr Wengam’s re-election reflected the confidence the Church had in his leadership and the work he had undertaken over the past four years. “You have earned that confidence through years of ministry, relationships that have been built across congregations, and work undertaken with your colleagues. Over the past four years, we have planted over 2,000 churches, and trained more than 440 pastors,” he said. The President noted that the achievements were the result of the collective commitment of ministers, congregations and communities that had embraced new missions and ministry opportunities. He said the second term offered the General Superintendent an opportunity to consolidate the gains made during his first tenure while ensuring that the benefits of the Church’s reforms reached congregations across the country. “A second term is a time to deepen worthwhile reforms and ensure that progress reaches the local congregations, including the small assemblies far from the national headquarters. “The confidence shown in your re-election also entails a renewed obligation to listen. May those who work closely with you feel free to offer honest advice and counsel.” President Mahama said the inauguration theme, “The Transformation Agenda Continues “ , anchored on the Six Rs: Reach, Rebuild, Restore, Reform, Reposition and Rebrand, challenged the Church to sustain its progress with patience and purpose. He observed that while the work of the Church was often celebrated from the pulpit, much of its ministry took place away from public attention through missionary journeys, counselling, visits to the sick and service to communities with limited resources. He therefore stressed the importance of prioritising the welfare of pastors and their families, including retired ministers who had devoted their lives to the Church. The President commended the First Lady and her Lordina Foundation for their support towards the healthcare needs of retired pastors through regular health screening exercises. “I salute my wife, First Lady Lordina Mahama, and her Lordina Foundation for the health screening ministry that they undertake every three months with retired pastors,” he said. “Their health screening, counselling, and medication have been a critical lifeline for many of our aged pastors.” President Mahama also underscored the need for strong administrative structures, transparent procedures, responsible financial management and effective leadership succession to ensure the Church’s long-term sustainability. He said the true measure of leadership was not only in the achievements recorded during one’s tenure but also in the people equipped to sustain the work after that leader had left office. The President further commended Rev. Dr Wengam for improving the public image and standing of the Assemblies of God, Ghana. “And I can speak confidently, Assemblies of God Ghana has become one of the most popular and most favoured Pentecostal denominations in Ghana,” the President said. He urged the Church to ensure that its efforts to reposition and rebrand the denomination were reflected in the experiences of members and visitors. “And so, as you continue your work of repositioning and rebranding the church, may the experience of those who enter its doors give meaning to its public image.” He expressed the hope that everyone who entered an Assemblies of God congregation would encounter a welcoming community, sound biblical teaching and support during difficult times. President Mahama also described the history of the Assemblies of God, Ghana, as a remarkable story of faith, perseverance and growth. Tracing its origins to Yendi in 1931, he said the Church had expanded across the country through the dedication of missionaries, Ghanaian ministers and committed congregations. With the denomination expected to celebrate its centenary in 2031, the President expressed confidence that the proposed Centenary Village project would be completed ahead of the milestone. “We shall build it to the glory of God. We honour all former generals, lieutenants, and all those whose service laid the foundation upon which today’s leadership is building,” he said. He stressed that institutions could only endure when successive generations received their inheritance with gratitude and built on it responsibly. Chairman of the World Assemblies of God Fellowship and General Superintendent of the Assemblies of God of Singapore, Reverend Dominic Yeo delivered the homily and conducted the inauguration ceremony. He charged Rev. Dr Wengam and the newly inaugurated Executive Presbytery to remain committed to advancing the Kingdom of God through the ministry of the Assemblies of God, Ghana. In his inaugural address, Rev. Dr Wengam pledged to accelerate the implementation of the Church’s Transformation Agenda, which is built around the Six Rs: Reach, Rebuild, Restore, Reform, Reposition and Rebrand. Other members of the Executive Presbytery inaugurated alongside him were Rev. Kwadwo Boateng Bempeh, Assistant General Superintendent; Rev. Albert Anane, General Secretary; and Rev. Dr Simon Abu Baba, General Treasurer.

items.title: Moyen-Mono : Kativou doté d’un forage et d’un réseau électrique
items.description: Tohoun, 8 nov. (ATOP) – Un forage et un réseau électrique ont été réceptionnés le samedi 7 novembre à Kativou, à 5 km au nord-est de Kpékplémé, dans la commune Moyen-Mono 2. Ces deux infrastructures, réalisées pour un coût total de 32 310 000 F CFA, viennent améliorer les conditions de vie des populations en facilitant l’accès à l’eau potable et à l’électricité. Les ouvrages ont été offerts par Miss Togo 2026, Eyou Prudence Angèle, avec l’appui financier de son partenaire Moov Africa. Le forage, d’une profondeur de 90 mètres, est équipé d’un château d’eau de 7 mètres de hauteur, d’un polytank d’une capacité de 2 m³, avec une possibilité d’extension de 2 m³ supplémentaires, et de trois robinets. Le réseau électrique, d’une puissance de 50 KVA, couvre une distance de 355 mètres. Ces réalisations visent à faciliter l’accès à l’eau potable et à améliorer l’éclairage du village. Elles offriront également aux élèves de meilleures conditions pour réviser leurs cours, notamment en soirée. La représentante de Moov Africa, Léaticia Sanvée, a expliqué que le choix de Kativou répond aux difficultés rencontrées par les ménages pour accéder à l’eau potable. Cette initiative vise à améliorer leurs conditions de vie, à réduire les infections liées à la consommation d’eau insalubre et à soutenir le développement local. Au nom des bénéficiaires, le préfet du Moyen-Mono, Colonel Gnakaoufré Yao Eindrè, et le maire de Moyen-Mono 2, Edou Zomblèwouh, ont salué le geste des donateurs. Ils se sont engagés à veiller au bon entretien des infrastructures et à leur utilisation judicieuse. ATOP/TM/YM/AO

items.title: Medeama extend home winning streaks to five with 1-0 victory over Swedru All Blacks
items.description: Medeama SC battled their way to a 1-0 win against Swedru All Blacks FC, maintaining their lead at the top of the Ghana Premier League (GPL) table at the TnA stadium in Tarkwa on Matchday 10. The Mauve and Yellow side took the lead in the 38th minute with an opener from number 19 centre forward Kingley Braye. The goal ignited the home crowd and set the tone for the rest of the match. Through tactical organisation, Medeama controlled the game leaving Swedru All Blacks without a way back. The defending champions extended their impressive winning streak on home soil, remaining unbeaten in Tarkwa this season. This victory keeps the Tarkwa-based side at the top of the table with 21 points, while Swedru All Blacks sit eighth with 14 points. The Black Magicians must regroup and pursue a return to winning ways. Meanwhile, Medeama remains confident in their relentless form as they aim to defend their title.

items.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : Ndèye Khady Anna Diatta offre au Sénégal sa troisième médaille d’or
items.description: Le Sénégal poursuit sa moisson de médailles d’or aux Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) Dakar 2026. Ndèye Khady Anna Diatta vient de décrocher le troisième titre olympique du pays hôte, à l’issue de son parcours victorieux en lutte de plage, dans la catégorie des moins de 45 kg. La jeune Sénégalaise confirme ainsi les espoirs placés en elle. Âgée de 17 ans, elle réalise un parcours remarquable avec un carton plein dans sa compétition, enchaînant les victoires face à ses adversaires. Porte-drapeau de la délégation sénégalaise lors de ces Jeux, Ndèye Khady Anna Diatta apporte une nouvelle consécration au Sénégal, après les titres remportés par Élisabeth Diatta chez les moins de 55 kg et Maguette Diop dans la catégorie des moins de 80 kg. Ce troisième sacre consacre également la performance de la lutte de plage sénégalaise, qui marque de son empreinte cette édition des JOJ organisée à domicile.

items.title: Train collision in Egypt's Giza kills 4, injures 88: health ministry
items.description: Two trains collided south of the Egyptian capital on Sunday, derailing several carriages, killing four and injuring dozens, according to the authorities. Egypt’s railway authority said a train travelling from Giza to Fayoum crashed into the rear of another service heading south from Cairo to the city of Aswan. The health ministry said an initial count put the toll from the crash at four passengers killed, with 88 others currently being treated for injuries in hospitals around the Giza area. State-owned media had earlier reported 120 people were wounded, without clarifying the degree of injury. President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said he was following the accident “with great concern”, and had directed authorities to conduct an urgent investigation to “hold accountable anyone found to have been negligent”. Emergency crews used cranes to remove the wreckage, the authority said. Authorities said they had launched an investigation into the cause of the crash, which occurred in Giza’s Al-Ayyat area, the site of Egypt’s worst-ever rail disaster. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar extended condolences to Egypt in the wake of the “tragic” accident, particularly the bereaved families. “Our thoughts and prayers are with those injured, and we wish them a swift and full recovery,” he said. “Pakistan stands in solidarity with Egypt and its people during this difficult time.” In 2002, more than 370 people were killed when a fire swept through a train carrying holiday travellers south of Cairo. In 2009, multiple train crashes in the area killed dozens . Egypt’s 110 million people depend heavily on rail transport, but the network — one of the largest in Africa — has suffered repeated deadly accidents . Over the past decade, Egypt has poured billions of dollars into updating its transport infrastructure, including new highways and high-speed rail lines, but has yet to overhaul much of its ageing rail network.

items.title: Two trains collide in Egypt, killing four people and injuring dozens more, authorities say
items.description: At least four people have been killed and nearly 90 injured after two trains collided in Egypt, the health ministry says. Several carriages were derailed after one train collided with the rear of another between Kafr Ammar and Al-Raqqa stations in Giza, near the capital Cairo, the Egyptian National Railways Authority said in a statement. Dozens of ambulances were dispatched to transport the injured to nearby hospitals, while cranes were deployed to remove the wreckage after traffic on the railroad was disrupted, Egyptian authorities said. The Egyptian railway system, the oldest in Africa and the Middle East, has a long history of deadly accidents, including when a train lost control while approaching the main station in Ramses, igniting a fire that killed 25 people. Another occurred in 2017 on the way to Alexandria, when a train derailed and collided head-on with another train, killing more than 40 people.
